title.zh: 卷二百一十四 列傳第一百三十九 藩鎮宣武彰義澤潞
title.en: Volume 214 Biographies 139: Buffer Regions: Xuanwu's Zhangyize Road
title.raw: 卷二百一十四 列傳第一百三十九 藩鎮宣武彰義澤潞 Volume 214 Biographies 139: Buffer Regions: Xuanwu's Zhangyize Road

sentences.zh: 藩鎮宣武彰義澤潞

translations.literal: Buffer Regions — Xuanwu, Zhangyi, and Zelu
translations.idiomatic: The buffer regions of Xuanwu, Zhangyi, and Zelu

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐，滑州匡城人。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanzuo was a native of Kuangcheng in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo was from Kuangcheng in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少倜蕩，不自業，為縣捕盜，犯法，吏笞辱幾死，乃亡命從永平軍，稍為牙將。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and unrestrained and would not settle to any trade. He served the county as a constable hunting bandits, broke the law, and was beaten and humiliated by officials nearly to death. He fled and joined the Yongping Army, gradually becoming a yak-commander.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was wild and idle. He worked as a county constable hunting bandits, broke the law, and was beaten nearly to death by the magistrate's men. He fled and enlisted in the Yongping Army, eventually becoming a junior guard officer.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，李靈耀據汴州反，玄佐乘其無備，襲取宋州，有詔以州遂隸其軍，節度使李勉即表署刺史。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, when Li Lingyao held Bian Prefecture in rebellion, Xuanzuo took advantage of his unpreparedness and seized Song Prefecture. An edict made the prefecture permanently part of his command, and the military governor Li Mian memorialized the court appointing him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali period Li Lingyao rebelled and held Bianzhou. Xuanzuo caught him unprepared and took Songzhou; an edict attached the prefecture to his command, and Governor Li Mian submitted a memorial appointing him prefect.

sentences.zh: 德宗建中初，進兼御史中丞，充宋、亳、潁節度使。

translations.literal: Early in the Jianzhong reign of Emperor Dezong he was promoted to concurrent Censor-in-Chief and appointed military governor of Song, Bo, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dezong's Jianzhong era he rose to Acting Censor-in-Chief and Military Commissioner of Song, Bo, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 時李納叛，李洧以徐州歸，納急攻之，詔玄佐援洧，大破納兵，斬首萬餘級，東南餉漕乃通。

translations.literal: When Li Na rebelled and Li Xu submitted Xuzhou, Na attacked Xu fiercely. The court ordered Xuanzuo to aid Xu. He defeated Na's army, beheading more than ten thousand, and grain transport from the southeast was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na rebelled and Li Xu brought Xuzhou back to the court, Na pressed the siege. Xuanzuo was ordered to relieve Xu, routed Na's forces with more than ten thousand heads taken, and southeastern supply convoys could move again.

sentences.zh: 進圍濮州，徇濮陽，皆下，再降其守將，遂通濮陽津。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Puzhou, pacified Puyang, took both, twice compelled their defenders to surrender, and reopened the Puyang crossing.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Puzhou and swept Puyang; both fell. He twice forced the garrison commanders to yield and reopened the ford at Puyang.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校兵部尚書、兼曹濮觀察、淄青兗鄆招討使、汴滑都統副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Minister of War, concurrent Inspector of Cao and Pu, Pacification Commissioner for Ziqing, Yan, and Yanzhou, and Deputy Supreme Commander of Bian and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Minister of War, Concurrent Observation Commissioner for Cao-Pu, Pacification Commissioner for Zi-Qing-Yan-Yan, and Deputy Supreme Commander of Bian-Hua.

sentences.zh: 李希烈之反，玄佐與李勉、陳少遊、哥舒曜聯兵屯淮、汝，數困賊。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie rebelled, Xuanzuo joined Li Mian, Chen Shaoyou, and Geshu Yao to camp on the Huai and Ru, repeatedly distressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rose, Xuanzuo allied with Li Mian, Chen Shaoyou, and Geshu Yao, massing troops on the Huai and Ru and repeatedly pinning the rebels.

sentences.zh: 帝在奉天，垂意關東，乃詔檢校尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Fengtian and concerned for the east; he was issued an edict Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor at Fengtian and his mind on the east, Xuanzuo was appointed Acting Left Vice Director and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 希烈攻陳州，玄佐救之，希烈走，遂進取汴州。

translations.literal: Xilie attacked Chenzhou; Xuanzuo relieved it; Xilie fled; he then advanced and took Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie besieged Chenzhou; Xuanzuo drove him off and pressed on to take Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔加汴宋節度使、陳州諸軍行營都統。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Military Governor of Bian-Song and Supreme Commander of all forces on campaign at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given Bian-Song governorship and overall command of the Chenzhou field armies.

sentences.zh: 玄佐本名洽，至是賜名以尊寵之。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo's original name was Qia; now it was changed by imperial gift to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Qia; the court now bestowed the name Xuanzuo as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 入朝，復兼涇原、四鎮、北庭兵馬副元帥，檢校司徒。

translations.literal: On entering court he was also made Deputy Grand Marshal of Jingyuan, the Four Garrisons, and Beiting, and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was additionally named Deputy Grand Marshal for Jingyuan, the Four Garrisons, and Beiting forces, and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 性豪縱，輕財好厚賞，故下益困。

translations.literal: He was bold and extravagant, careless with money and fond of lavish rewards, so his subordinates grew only more impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant by nature and quick to spend on rich rewards, he left his men all the harder pressed.

sentences.zh: 汴自李忠臣以來，士卒驕，不能自還，至玄佐彌甚。

translations.literal: Since Li Zhongchen's time the troops at Bian had been unruly and could not be checked; under Xuanzuo this worsened.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Zhongchen onward the Bian soldiery had grown insubordinate; under Xuanzuo the disorder deepened.

sentences.zh: 其後殺帥長，大鈔劫，狃於利而然也。

translations.literal: Later they murdered their commanders and looted on a grand scale, habituated to profit.
translations.idiomatic: They went on to kill their commanders and mount great plunder—accustomed to gain and reckless of restraint.

sentences.zh: 玄佐貴，母尚在，賢婦人也。

translations.literal: When Xuanzuo rose high his mother was still alive, a worthy woman.
translations.idiomatic: Though now a great lord, he still had his mother—a woman of real virtue.

sentences.zh: 常月織絁一端，示不忘本。

translations.literal: Every month she wove a bolt of coarse silk to show she had not forgotten her origins.
translations.idiomatic: Each month she wove a bolt of coarse cloth, a reminder never to forget where they came from.

sentences.zh: 數教敕玄佐盡臣節。

translations.literal: Again and again she admonished Xuanzuo to perform his duties as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: She repeatedly urged him to observe full loyalty toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 見縣令走廷中白事，退，戒曰：「長吏恐懼卑甚。

translations.literal: Seeing the magistrate run into the hall to report, she withdrew and warned: "Your chief official is terribly afraid and abject.
translations.idiomatic: Once she saw a county magistrate hurry in to report; when he left she warned her son, "That magistrate was terribly cowed.

sentences.zh: 吾思而父吏於縣，亦當爾。

translations.literal: I think how your father served as a county official—he must have been treated just so.
translations.idiomatic: I remember your father in county office; no doubt he was humbled the same way.

sentences.zh: 而據案當之，可安乎？」

translations.literal: Yet you sit at your desk and accept this—can that be right?"
translations.idiomatic: And you sit above him as if that were natural—is that seemly?"

sentences.zh: 玄佐感悟，故待下益加禮。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo was moved and thereafter treated his subordinates with greater courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo took the lesson to heart and afterward showed his subordinates more respect.

sentences.zh: 汴有相國寺，或傳佛軀汗流，玄佐自往大施金帛，於是將吏、商賈奔走輸金錢，惟恐後。

translations.literal: Bian had the Xiangguo Temple; rumor spread that the Buddha-image was sweating. Xuanzuo went in person and gave vast gifts of gold and silk, and officers, clerks, and merchants rushed to pour in money lest they be last.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xiangguo Monastery word went around that the Buddha's body was sweating. Xuanzuo went himself and gave lavish gold and silk; officers, traders, and merchants vied to donate for fear of coming late.

sentences.zh: 十日，玄佐敕止，籍所入得巨萬，因以贍軍。

translations.literal: After ten days Xuanzuo ordered a halt and registered the takings—an enormous sum—which he then used to pay the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day he called the gifts in, tallied an immense haul, and turned it to army pay.

sentences.zh: 其權譎類若此。

translations.literal: His cunning schemes were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the kind of stratagem he favored.

sentences.zh: 初，李納遣使至汴，玄佐盛飾女子進之，厚饋遺，皆得其陰謀，故納最憚之。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Na had sent envoys to Bian; Xuanzuo lavished ornamented women on them and gave rich gifts, learning all their secret designs, so that Na feared him most.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Na sent envoys to Bian, Xuanzuo entertained them with lavishly adorned women and rich presents and learned their whole plot—so Na feared him above all.

sentences.zh: 所寵吏張士南及假子樂士朝貲皆鉅萬；

translations.literal: His favored clerk Zhang Shinan and his adopted son Yue Shichao each amassed fortunes in the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: His favorite clerk Zhang Shinan and adopted son Yue Shichao each piled up wealth in the millions;

sentences.zh: 而士朝私玄佐嬖妾，懼事覺，冘玄佐，死，年五十八，贈太傅，謚曰壯武。

translations.literal: but Shichao had an affair with Xuanzuo's concubine; fearing exposure he poisoned Xuanzuo. He died at fifty-eight, posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the posthumous name Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Shichao had secretly taken one of Xuanzuo's concubines; afraid he would be found out he poisoned him. Xuanzuo died at fifty-eight and was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 軍中匿喪俟代，帝亦為隱。

translations.literal: The army concealed his death awaiting a successor; the emperor colluded in the concealment.
translations.idiomatic: The army hid his death while waiting for a replacement; the court winked at it.

sentences.zh: 逾三日乃發喪。

translations.literal: Not until three days later was the mourning announced.
translations.idiomatic: Three days passed before the obsequies were made public.

sentences.zh: 使至，帝問所欲立，曰：「陜虢觀察使吳湊可乎？」

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived the emperor asked whom they wished to install. They said: "Would Shaanxi-Guo Observation Commissioner Wu Cou be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy came the emperor asked whom they wanted. They answered, "Would Wu Cou of Shaanxi-Guo do?"

sentences.zh: 監軍孟介、行軍盧瑗以為便，乃拜湊為節度使。

translations.literal: Military overseer Meng Jie and staff officer Lu Yuan approved; Wu Cou was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The army overseer Meng Jie and Chief of Staff Lu Yuan agreed, and Cou was commissioned governor.

sentences.zh: 至汜水，玄佐柩將遷，士請具禮，瑗不許，眾皆怒。

translations.literal: At Sishui, as Xuanzuo's bier was about to be moved, the troops asked full rites; Yuan refused and all were enraged.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui, when the coffin was to be moved, the soldiers demanded full honors; Yuan refused and the men flared up.

sentences.zh: 陵晨，甲而噪，起玄佐子士寧於喪，使坐重榻，墨其衣，尊為留後，殺大將曹金岸、浚儀令李邁，醢之，唯瑗、介獲免。

translations.literal: At dawn they donned armor and clamored, raised Xuanzuo's son Shining on the bier to a high couch, blackened his garments, proclaimed him acting commander, slew the great generals Cao Jin'an and Lingyi Magistrate Li Mai, pickled them, sparing only Yuan and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the men armed and shouted, set Shining on the coffin on a high seat, smeared his clothes with ink, hailed him leave-behind commander, killed Generals Cao Jin'an and Magistrate Li Mai of Lingyi, salted their corpses, and spared Yuan and Jie alone.

sentences.zh: 士寧乃出貯財分勞吏士。

translations.literal: Shining then drew on stored wealth to reward officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shining opened the treasury and rewarded the officers and ranks.

sentences.zh: 介以聞，帝召宰相計議，竇參曰：「汴人挾李納以邀命，若不許，勢且合，不可解。」

translations.literal: Jie reported this; the emperor called the chief ministers to counsel. Dou Can said: "The men of Bian are holding Li Na's name over the court—if we refuse they will surely unite and the knot cannot be undone."
translations.idiomatic: Jie reported in; the emperor convened the council. Dou Can said, "The Bian troops are using Li Na to hold the court hostage—refuse them and they will surely join him and the affair will be beyond remedy."

sentences.zh: 遂以士寧為左金吾衛將軍，嗣節度。

translations.literal: Shining was therefore made General of the Left Golden Crown Guard and succeeded to the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Shining was made Left Golden-Crown Guard General and confirmed as governor.

sentences.zh: 始，玄佐養子士幹與士朝皆來京師，士幹知玄佐死無狀，遣奴持刀紿為吊，入殺士朝於次。

translations.literal: Earlier Xuanzuo's adopted sons Shigan and Shichao had both come to the capital. Learning that Xuanzuo's death was suspicious, Shigan sent a slave with a dagger feigning condolences and killed Shichao in the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo's adopted sons Shigan and Shichao had been in the capital. Shigan, suspecting foul play in his father's death, sent a servant with a blade under pretense of mourning and killed Shichao in his quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其專，亦賜士幹死。

translations.literal: The emperor detested his arrogation of authority and condemned Shigan to death as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abhorred his private justice and had Shigan executed too.

sentences.zh: 士寧未授詔時，私遣人結王武俊、劉濟、田緒等，諸鎮不直之，皆執其使。

translations.literal: Before his commission arrived Shining had secretly sent men to win over Wang Wujun, Liu Ji, Tian Xu, and others; the other provinces disapproved and all seized his envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict reached him Shining secretly contacted Wang Wujun, Liu Ji, Tian Xu, and others; the other fiefs would not support him and detained every envoy.

sentences.zh: 而士寧忍暴，嘗手殺人杯案間；

translations.literal: Shining was cruel and violent; he would kill men with his own hand across the banquet table;
translations.idiomatic: He was brutal—sometimes killing guests at table with his own hand;

sentences.zh: 又強烝父諸妾，逼吏民妻女亂之，或裸而觀；

translations.literal: he forced himself on his father's concubines and ravished officials' and commoners' wives and daughters, sometimes making them strip for onlookers;
translations.idiomatic: he violated his father's concubines and took officials' and commoners' women by force, sometimes making them perform naked;

sentences.zh: 每畋獵，數日乃還。

translations.literal: on hunts he would be gone many days before returning.
translations.idiomatic: when he hunted he stayed out for days on end.

sentences.zh: 其下厭苦不服。

translations.literal: His subordinates grew weary and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: His men wearied of him and would not stand behind him.

sentences.zh: 大將李萬榮者，故與玄佐同裏相善，寬厚得士心。

translations.literal: Great General Li Wanrong had been a fellow townsman and friend of Xuanzuo, broad-minded and trusted by the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanrong, once Xuanzuo's neighbor and friend, was generous and held the soldiers' regard.

sentences.zh: 士寧忌之，奪其兵，使攝州事。

translations.literal: Shining envied him, stripped him of his command, and put him in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shining feared him, took away his troops, and left him administering the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗引眾二萬畋城南，未還，萬榮晨入府，召所留親兵告曰：「天子有詔召大夫，俾我代節度。

translations.literal: Once Shining led twenty thousand men to hunt south of the city and had not returned; Wanrong entered the headquarters at dawn, summoned the loyal detachments left behind and said: "The Son of Heaven has an edict calling the commissioner—I am to replace him as governor.
translations.idiomatic: With Shining hunting south of the city with twenty thousand men, Wanrong entered headquarters at dawn, called the loyal troops in garrison and announced, "The Son of Heaven has recalled the commissioner—I am your new governor.

sentences.zh: 人賜錢三萬。」

translations.literal: Each man is granted thirty thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: Every soldier will receive thirty thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 士皆拜。

translations.literal: The men all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The men bowed assent.

sentences.zh: 於是分兵閉諸門，使告士寧曰：「詔書召大夫，宜速去，不然，事急且傳首以獻。」

translations.literal: He then posted troops to close every gate and sent word to Shining: "An edict summons the commissioner—leave at once, or we will send your head up as a gift."
translations.idiomatic: Troops sealed the gates and a messenger told Shining, "The edict calls you—go quickly, or in haste we may present your head."

sentences.zh: 士寧知眾不與，將五百騎出奔，次中牟，亡者已半，至東都，惟僮妾數十人從之。

translations.literal: Knowing the army was not his, Shining fled with five hundred horsemen; at Zhongmu half had deserted; at the eastern capital only a few dozen slave-girls followed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he had no support Shining fled with five hundred horse; by Zhongmu half his following was gone; at Luoyang only a handful of concubines remained.

sentences.zh: 既至京師，詔就第，禁出入。

translations.literal: Once in the capital he was ordered to stay in his residence and forbidden to go abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he was confined to his house and forbidden to leave.

sentences.zh: 萬榮斬其支附數十人，以二十萬緡勞軍，詔籍士寧家貲給之。

translations.literal: Wanrong executed several dozen of Shining's partisans and spent two hundred thousand strings in cash to reward the army; an edict ordered Shining's family property inventoried to pay for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong executed dozens of Shining's adherents and paid the army two hundred thousand strings from the treasury; the court ordered Shining's estate seized to cover the cost.

sentences.zh: 拜萬榮兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Wanrong was made Acting Commander of Troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong was appointed acting commander of forces.

sentences.zh: 於是藉驕兵數百人，悉遣西防秋，當戍者怨之。

translations.literal: He then registered several hundred unruly soldiers and sent them all west on autumn defense; those due to rotate out resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He listed hundreds of unruly troops for western autumn garrison; men slated for duty grumbled.

sentences.zh: 大校韓惟清、張彥琳等請往，不許，使其子乃將，未行，彥琳等因其怨，誘使反攻萬榮，不勝，劫運財、民貲，殺掠數千人而潰。

translations.literal: Senior commanders Han Weiqing and Zhang Yanlin asked to lead them; permission was refused and Wanrong's son Nai was sent instead. Before they marched Yanlin and the others, nursing resentment, incited a counter-attack on Wanrong; they failed, looted transport funds and civilian property, killed and plundered thousands, then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Han Weiqing and Zhang Yanlin asked to lead the detachment but were refused—Wanrong's son Nai was put in command. Before marching, Yanlin exploited the men's anger and turned them on Wanrong; beaten, they seized convoy money and civilian wealth, slew and robbed thousands, and broke up.

sentences.zh: 惟清奔鄭州，彥琳走東都自歸，有詔宥死竄惡地。

translations.literal: Weiqing fled to Zhengzhou; Yanlin went to Luoyang and surrendered; an edict pardoned them but exiled them to harsh regions.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing fled to Zhengzhou; Yanlin surrendered at Luoyang; both were spared death but banished to the frontier wastes.

sentences.zh: 殘士奔宋州，劉逸淮撫之，萬榮悉誅其妻子，以故眾不安，或呼於市曰：「大軍至，城且破。」

translations.literal: The remnant troops fled to Songzhou; Liu Yihuai pacified them; Wanrong executed all their wives and children, so the men were unsettled; some cried in the market: "The great army is coming—the city will fall."
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled to Songzhou and Liu Yihuai took them in; Wanrong killed every family they had left behind, and the troops grew restless; someone shouted in the market that a host was coming to break the city."

sentences.zh: 萬榮捕按之，或言為士寧所教，萬榮斬之，以狀聞，故士寧斥置郴州。

translations.literal: Wanrong hunted them down; some said Shining had taught them; Wanrong beheaded them and reported; therefore Shining was banished to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wanrong arrested and interrogated them; some said Shining had stirred them up; he executed the prisoners and reported up, and Shining was exiled to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄進萬榮節度使。

translations.literal: Soon Wanrong was promoted to full Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wanrong received the full governorship.

sentences.zh: 會病甚，以兵屬鄧惟恭。

translations.literal: When he fell gravely ill he handed the army to Deng Weigong.
translations.idiomatic: Falling seriously ill he transferred the forces to Deng Weigong.

sentences.zh: 惟恭者，與萬榮同里閈。

translations.literal: Weigong was from the same neighborhood as Wanrong.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong came from Wanrong's own ward.

sentences.zh: 而署子乃為司馬，出大將李湛、張伾、伊婁涚等於外，欲殺之，不果。

translations.literal: But his appointed son Nai served as Chief of Staff; he sent great generals Li Zhan, Zhang Pi, and Yilou Sui abroad intending to kill them, but failed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nai, named regent, was Chief of Staff; Wanrong had posted Generals Li Zhan, Zhang Pi, and Yilou Sui outside hoping to kill them, but could not.

sentences.zh: 萬榮死，是夜惟恭與監軍俱文珍執乃送京師，杖死京兆府，以董晉代之。

translations.literal: When Wanrong died that night Weigong and the army overseer Ju Wenzhen seized Nai and sent him to the capital; he was beaten to death in the Jingzhao office; Dong Jin replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: The night Wanrong died Weigong and Army Overseer Ju Wenzhen seized Nai, sent him to court, and had him flogged to death in Jingzhao; Dong Jin took the command.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠，幽州潞人，以世蔭為諸王府戶曹參軍事。

translations.literal: Wu Shaoqing was a native of Lu in Youzhou, entering office by hereditary privilege as Registrar of the Princes' Households.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoqing came from Lu in Youzhou and entered office by inherited privilege as Registrar in the Princes' Households.

sentences.zh: 客荊南，節度使庾準器之，留為牙門將。

translations.literal: As a traveler in Jingnan, Military Governor Yu Zhun prized him and kept him as a yak-commander.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Jingnan, Governor Yu Zhun took him in and made him a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 從入朝，道襄陽，度梁崇義必叛，密畫計，將獻天子，而李希烈以其事聞，有詔嘉美，擢封通義郡王。

translations.literal: Returning with Zhun to court, he passed Xiangyang, judged that Liang Chongyi would surely rebel, and secretly drew up a plan to present to the Son of Heaven; Li Xilie reported his scheme; an edict praised him and he was enfeoffed Prince of Tongyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to court he passed Xiangyang, decided Liang Chongyi would rebel, and drafted a secret plan for the throne; Li Xilie exposed it—but an edict praised him and raised him to Prince of Tongyi.

sentences.zh: 崇義反，希烈以少誠為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Chongyi rebelled Xilie made Shaoqing his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyi rose, Xilie made Shaoqing his van.

sentences.zh: 事平，賜實封戶五十。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was given fifty households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: After peace he received a fifty-household substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 希烈叛，少誠為盡力，及死，推陳仙奇主後務，既又殺之，眾乃共推少誠，德宗因授申、蔡、光等州節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Xilie rebelled Shaoqing gave his utmost; after Xilie's death he pushed Chen Xianqi to handle affairs, then killed him too; the troops together raised Shaoqing; Dezong therefore appointed him Acting Military and Observation Commissioner of Shen, Cai, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie rebelled he fought hard; after Xilie's death he backed Chen Xianqi, then killed him; the men chose Shaoqing and Dezong made him Acting Governor of Shen, Cai, and Guang.

sentences.zh: 少誠為治，能儉損，完軍實。

translations.literal: Shaoqing's administration was frugal and he repaired military stores.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, Shaoqing was sparing and rebuilt the army's stores.

sentences.zh: 自希烈以來，申、蔡人劫於苛法而忘所歸，及耆長既物故，則壯者習見暴掠，恬於搏鬥。

translations.literal: Since Xilie's time the people of Shen and Cai had been harried by harsh laws and forgot where loyalty lay; once the elders died the younger men knew only plunder and grew accustomed to fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xilie Shen and Cai had been ground down by harsh rule; when the old leading families passed away the young knew only raiding and took combat lightly.

sentences.zh: 地少馬，乘騾以戰，號「騾子軍」，尤悍銳。

translations.literal: The region had few horses; they rode mules into battle and were called the "Mule Army," especially fierce and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Horses were scarce—they fought mounted on mules in what was called the "Mule Army," notoriously fierce.

sentences.zh: 甲皆畫雷公星文以厭勝，詛詈王師。

translations.literal: Their armor bore the Thunder Lord and stellar talismans for victory; they cursed the imperial armies.
translations.idiomatic: They painted Thunder Lord and star signs on their armor as charms and cursed the court's troops.

sentences.zh: 其屬鄭常、楊冀欲劫少誠，逐之以聽命，不克，常、冀被害。

translations.literal: His officers Zheng Chang and Yang Ji wished to seize Shaoqing and drive him out to obey the throne; they failed and Chang and Ji were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates Zheng Chang and Yang Ji tried to capture Shaoqing and expel him in submission to the court; the plot failed and both died.

sentences.zh: 少誠盡宥諸將，以結眾心。

translations.literal: Shaoqing pardoned all the generals to bind the men to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing forgave every general involved to keep the corps united.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，進拜節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was promoted to full Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 5 he received the full governorship.

sentences.zh: 久之，曲環卒，少誠間陳許無帥，以兵攻臨潁，戍將韋清與賊通，留後上官涚遣兵三千救之，悉為賊俘，遂圍許州。

translations.literal: After a long while Qu Huan died; Shaoqing judged Chen Xu leaderless and attacked Linying; the garrison commander Wei Qing colluded with the rebels; Acting Governor Shangguan Sui sent three thousand to relieve the town—all were captured—and they besieged Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Qu Huan died; Shaoqing thought Chen Xu had no chief, attacked Linying, found the commander Wei Qing in league with the enemy, and though Acting Governor Shangguan Sui sent three thousand all were taken; then they besieged Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗怒，削少誠官爵，合十六道兵進討。

translations.literal: Dezong in anger stripped Shaoqing of rank and titles and mobilized sixteen circuits against him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Dezong removed Shaoqing's offices and ordered sixteen commands to advance against him.

sentences.zh: 於頔以襄陽兵戰吳房、朗山，禽其三將。

translations.literal: Yu Di with Xiangyang troops fought at Wufang and Langshan and took three of Shaoqing's generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di's Xiangyang force fought at Wufang and Langshan and captured three rebel generals.

sentences.zh: 王宗以壽州兵破賊於秋柵。

translations.literal: Wang Zong with Shouzhou troops defeated the rebels at Qiu Fence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zong's Shouzhou troops routed them at Qiu Fence stockade.

sentences.zh: 於時師雖眾，無統帥，而宦人監軍顓進退，互為異見。

translations.literal: By then the allied hosts were many but had no supreme commander; eunuch army overseers directed advances and retreats and disputed one another.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies were huge yet leaderless; eunuch overseers held the reins and quarreled.

sentences.zh: 既戰小溵河，諸道師未交而潰，棄輜杖不貲。

translations.literal: After a skirmish at the Xiaobin River the columns had not yet met the enemy when they broke and abandoned baggage and arms beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xiaobin engagement the columns broke before joining battle and cast away supplies in heaps.

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔夏州節度使韓全義為淮蔡招討處置使，上官涚副之，諸將皆受節度。

translations.literal: The emperor then made Xiaye Military Governor Han Quanyi Pacification and Disposition Commissioner for Huai-Cai, with Shangguan Sui as deputy; all generals accepted his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong named Han Quanyi of Xiaye Pacification Commissioner for Huai-Cai with Shangguan Sui as deputy; every commander fell under his command.

sentences.zh: 與賊吳少陽等戰廣利城，師復敗，退營五樓，為賊所乘，遂大潰。

translations.literal: Fighting Wu Shaoyang and others at Guangli City the host was beaten again, withdrew to camp at Wulou, was pressed by the rebels, and routed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Against Wu Shaoyang and others at Guanglichuan they lost again, fell back to Wulou, were overrun, and collapsed completely.

sentences.zh: 全義及監軍賈英秀等夜遯保溵水。

translations.literal: Quanyi and army overseer Jia Yingxiu fled by night to secure Linshui.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi and Overseer Jia Yingxiu fled by night to Linshui.

sentences.zh: 汴宋、徐泗、淄青兵走陳州。

translations.literal: Bian-Song, Xu-Si, and Ziqing troops retreated to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Troops of Bian-Song, Xu-Si, and Ziqing fell back to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 少誠薄溵水而營，全義懼，退保陳，而潞、滑、河陽、河中兵逃歸，唯陳許將孟元陽、神策將蘇光榮壁溵水。

translations.literal: Shaoqing camped close to Linshui; Quanyi was afraid and withdrew to Chen; Lu, Hua, Heyang, and Hezhong troops fled home; only Chen Xu generals Meng Yuanyang and Shence general Su Guangrong held Linshui.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing pitched camp near Linshui; Quanyi in fear pulled back to Chen; armies of Lu, Hua, Heyang, and Hezhong scattered home; only Meng Yuanyang of Chen-Xu and Su Guangrong of the Shence Corps held at Linshui.

sentences.zh: 全義乃斬潞將夏侯仲宣、滑將時昂、河陽將權文度、河中將郭湘，欲以振師，不能也。

translations.literal: Quanyi then executed Lu commander Xia Houzhongxuan, Hua commander Shi Ang, Heyang commander Quan Wendu, and Hezhong commander Guo Xiang to shake the army—but could not.
translations.idiomatic: He executed commanders Xia Houzhongxuan of Lu, Shi Ang of Hua, Quan Wendu of Heyang, and Guo Xiang of Hezhong to steady morale—and failed.

sentences.zh: 少誠引兵去。

translations.literal: Shaoqing withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing then led his force away.

sentences.zh: 全義之敗，少誠得帳中諸公書數百番，持以紿眾曰：「朝廷公卿托全義破蔡日掠將士妻女為婢媵。」

translations.literal: After Quanyi's defeat Shaoqing took several hundred letters from the command tent of the court's grandees and held them before the troops: "The court's chief ministers entrusted Quanyi, on the day Cai was broken, to seize our officers' wives and daughters as bondmaids."
translations.idiomatic: In defeat Shaoqing seized hundreds of letters from grandees in Quanyi's tent and told the men, "The court's ministers told Quanyi that when Cai fell he might seize your wives and daughters as concubines."

sentences.zh: 以激怒其眾，絕向順意。

translations.literal: Thus he enraged them and cut off every thought of submission.
translations.idiomatic: With that he inflamed them and killed any wish to submit.

sentences.zh: 少誠弱王師，移書於英秀求昭雪。

translations.literal: Taking the court armies lightly, he wrote Yingxiu asking vindication.
translations.idiomatic: Contemptuous of the imperial forces, he wrote Yingxiu begging clearance.

sentences.zh: 帝召大臣議，宰相賈耽曰：「五樓軍退，而少誠卷甲不追，有自新路。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the ministers; Chief Minister Jia Dan said: "After the retreat at Wulou Shaoqing sheathed his arms and did not pursue—a sign he seeks a new path."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor convened ministers; Jia Dan said, "After Wulou he did not pursue—that shows he wants another road."

sentences.zh: 帝意稍挺，少誠復固巢穴矣。

translations.literal: The emperor's will stiffened slightly and Shaoqing entrenched himself again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented a little and Shaoqing dug in once more.

sentences.zh: 然猶以宦者監諸道軍。

translations.literal: Yet eunuchs still oversaw the allied armies.
translations.idiomatic: Still eunuchs supervised the allied hosts.

sentences.zh: 劍南韋臯上言，以為不如擇重臣為統帥，因薦渾瑊、賈耽，「陛下若重煩元老，更求其次，則臣請以銳士萬人順流趨荊、楚，可以攘翦元憝。

translations.literal: Wei Gao of Jiannan memorialized that it would be better to choose a weighty minister as commander-in-chief and recommended Hun Jian and Jia Dan: "If Your Majesty does not wish to burden the elders again, I next ask leave to lead ten thousand elite troops downriver toward Jing and Chu and cut down the chief rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao of Jiannan urged appointing a senior commander instead, naming Hun Jian and Jia Dan: "If Your Majesty will not trouble the elders again, let me take ten thousand picked men down the Yangtze toward Jing-Chu and strike the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 不然，因其請罪，特加原洗，罷兩河諸軍，亦其次也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, when he pleads guilty, grant special pardon and disband the armies of the two He regions—that would be the next best course.
translations.idiomatic: Or, when he sues for pardon, wash his offenses specially and stand down the He armies—that would be second best.

sentences.zh: 使少誠禍盈惡周，變生帳下，必其賊黨，又當以官爵與之，則一少誠死，一少誠生，亦何足賴？」

translations.literal: If Shaocheng's calamity overflows and his wickedness runs full circle, mutiny arises beneath his tent—it will surely be his own villainous faction; they will again be given office and rank; then one Shaocheng dies and another Shaocheng is born—what is there to rely upon?"
translations.idiomatic: Let Shaocheng's evil brim over until rebellion breaks out in his own camp—it will be the same rebel clique, rewarded again with offices and titles; one Shaocheng dies, another rises in his place—what could we trust in that?"

sentences.zh: 帝遂赦少誠，盡還其官爵。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Shaocheng and fully restored his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took it and pardoned Shaocheng, restoring every office and title.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，進同中書門下平章事，檢校司空，徙封濮陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, [he] was promoted to Co-Grand Councilor through the Chancellery, Acting Minister of Works, and transferred to the title Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong succeeded, he rose to co-grand councilor, Acting Minister of Works, and was reassigned as Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 元和四年死，贈司徒，而吳少陽代之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he died; posthumously [given] Situ; and Wu Shaoyang replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanhe 4 (809); the court posthumously named him Minister over the Masses, and Wu Shaoyang took his place.

sentences.zh: 少陽者，滄州清池人。

translations.literal: Shaoyang was a man of Qingchi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyang was from Qingchi in Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與少誠同在魏博軍，相友善。

translations.literal: He and Shaocheng were together in the Weibo Army and were friendly with each other.
translations.idiomatic: He and Shaocheng had served together in the Weibo Army and were close friends.

sentences.zh: 少誠得淮西，多出金帛邀之，養以為弟，署右職，親近無間。

translations.literal: When Shaocheng obtained Huai West, he spent much gold and silk to win him over, raised him as a younger brother, appointed him to a high post, and was close to him without estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shaocheng held Huai West, he lavished gold and silk to draw him in, treated him as a sworn younger brother, gave him a senior command, and kept him at his side without reserve.

sentences.zh: 少陽度少誠猜忍，且畏禍，請為外捍，少誠乃表為申州刺史。

translations.literal: Shaoyang reckoned that Shaocheng was suspicious and cruel, and also feared calamity; he requested to serve as outer defense, and Shaocheng thereupon memorialized to make him prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyang judged that Shaocheng was suspicious and ruthless, and feared what might befall him; he asked to serve on the outer line of defense, and Shaocheng memorialized to appoint him prefect of Shen.

sentences.zh: 為治尚寬易，舉軍附賴。

translations.literal: In governing he favored leniency and ease; the whole army attached itself to and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was easy and lenient, and the whole army came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 少誠病亟，家奴單於熊兒矯召少陽至，攝副使，總軍事，於是殺少誠子元慶，自稱留後。

translations.literal: When Shaocheng was critically ill, the household slave Shan Yu Xiong'er forged a summons for Shaoyang to come, acted as vice commissioner, and took overall military affairs; thereupon he killed Shaocheng's son Yuanqing and styled himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaocheng fell gravely ill, his household slave Shan Yu Xiong'er forged a summons for Shaoyang, assumed the vice commissionership and command of the army, killed Shaocheng's son Yuanqing, and declared himself acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以王承宗方叛，故詔遂王為節度使，以少陽領留後。

translations.literal: Because Xianzong [knew that] Wang Chengzong was then in rebellion, he therefore issued an edict making Wang military commissioner at once, and had Shaoyang hold the acting commission.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Chengzong was in open revolt, Xianzong promptly confirmed Wang as military commissioner and let Shaoyang serve as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 居三年，進拜節度使。

translations.literal: After three years in office, he was promoted and invested as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was formally appointed military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 少陽不立繇役籍，隨日賦斂於人。

translations.literal: Shaoyang did not establish corvée registers; he levied and collected from the people day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyang kept no corvée rolls and simply taxed the people as each day demanded.

sentences.zh: 地多原澤，益畜馬。

translations.literal: The land had many plains and marshes; he further raised horses.
translations.idiomatic: The region was rich in open country and marshland, and he bred horses in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 時時掠壽州茶山，劫商賈，招四方亡命，以實其軍。

translations.literal: From time to time he plundered the tea hills of Shouzhou, robbed merchants, and recruited fugitives from all quarters to fill out his army.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly raided the tea hills of Shou, preyed on merchants, and gathered outlaws from every direction to strengthen his forces.

sentences.zh: 不肯朝，然屢獻牧馬以自解，帝亦因善之。

translations.literal: He would not come to court, yet repeatedly presented pastured horses to excuse himself; the Emperor also therefore treated him favorably.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to attend court, but sent tribute horses again and again by way of apology, and the Emperor came to look on him with favor.

sentences.zh: 九年死，子元濟匿不發喪，以病聞，偽表請元濟主兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; his son Yuanji concealed [the death] and did not announce mourning, reported illness, and submitted a false memorial asking that Yuanji command the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of his rule he died; his son Yuanji hid the death, reported only that he was ill, and forged a memorial asking that Yuanji be allowed to take command.

sentences.zh: 帝遣太醫往視，即陽言少愈，不得見。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the imperial physician to examine him; [Yuanji] at once falsely said [Shaoyang] was somewhat recovered and would not permit a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent the court physician to examine him; Yuanji promptly claimed Shaoyang was improving and refused a visit.

sentences.zh: 元濟者，其長子也，山首燕頷，垂頤，鼻長六寸。

translations.literal: Yuanji was his eldest son; he had a lofty brow and swallow jaw, a hanging chin, and a nose six inches long.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was his eldest son—a towering brow, a swallow's jaw, a heavy jowl, and a nose six inches long.

sentences.zh: 始仕，試協律郎，攝蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: When he first entered service, he was tried as Director of Harmonization, acting prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a probationary Director of Harmonization and acting prefect of Cai.

sentences.zh: 有董重質者，少誠婿也，勇悍，久將，善為兵，元濟倚之，因說元濟，請以精兵三千由壽之間道取揚州，東約李師道以舟師襲潤州，據之；

translations.literal: There was Dong Chongzhi, Shaocheng's son-in-law—fierce and bold, long a commander, skilled at warfare; Yuanji relied on him, and therefore urged Yuanji, requesting to take three thousand elite troops by a hidden route through Shou to seize Yangzhou, and in the east arrange with Li Shidao that naval forces raid Runzhou and hold it;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi, Shaocheng's son-in-law, was fierce in battle, a veteran commander, and skilled in war; Yuanji leaned on him, and Chongzhi urged him to take three thousand picked men by a secret route from Shou to seize Yangzhou, while in the east Li Shidao's fleet would strike Run and hold it;

sentences.zh: 遣奇兵掩商、鄧，取嚴綬，進守襄陽，以搖東南，則荊、衡、黔、巫傳一矢可定，五嶺非朝廷所有。

translations.literal: Send extraordinary troops to surprise Shang and Deng, capture Yan Shou, advance and hold Xiangyang to shake the southeast—then Jing, Heng, Qian, and Wu would fall at the report of a single arrow, and the Five Ridges would no longer belong to the court.
translations.idiomatic: send raiders to strike Shang and Deng, capture Yan Shou, and push on to hold Xiangyang, unsettling the southeast; then Jing, Heng, Qian, and Wu would topple at a rumor, and the Five Ridges would slip from the court's grasp.

sentences.zh: 又請輕兵五百，自領三日襲東都，則天下騷動，可以橫行。

translations.literal: He further requested five hundred light troops, personally to lead a three-day raid on the Eastern Capital—then the realm would be in uproar and he could rampage at will.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for five hundred light troops to lead himself in a three-day strike on the Eastern Capital; the empire would convulse, and they could sweep all before them.

sentences.zh: 元濟猶豫不能用。

translations.literal: Yuanji hesitated and did not adopt [the plan].
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji wavered and would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 先是，其屬蘇兆、楊元卿、侯惟清嘗勸少陽入朝，或言其有異志，元濟縊兆，歸其屍，而囚惟清。

translations.literal: Earlier, his subordinates Su Zhao, Yang Yuanqing, and Hou Weiqing had urged Shaoyang to enter court; some said they harbored divergent intent; Yuanji strangled Zhao, returned his corpse, and imprisoned Weiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his officers Su Zhao, Yang Yuanqing, and Hou Weiqing had urged Shaoyang to come to court; when some accused them of disloyalty, Yuanji had Zhao strangled and his body sent back, and Weiqing thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 帝以二人者皆死，故贈惟清兵部尚書，兆尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Because both men were dead, the Emperor posthumously granted Weiqing Minister of War and Zhao Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When both were dead, the Emperor posthumously honored Weiqing as Minister of War and Zhao as Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 時元卿奏事在長安，見宰相李吉甫，具言淮西事，且請蔡使在道者，隨在所系之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanqing was in Chang'an reporting on affairs; he saw the chief minister Li Jifu, fully explained Huai West matters, and further requested that Cai envoys on the road be detained wherever found.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing was then in Chang'an on court business; he saw Chief Minister Li Jifu, laid out the whole Huai West situation, and asked that any Cai envoy on the road be arrested on the spot.

sentences.zh: 少陽死四十日，帝不為輟朝，易將增戍以須變。

translations.literal: Forty days after Shaoyang's death, the Emperor did not suspend court for mourning; he changed commanders and increased garrisons to await developments.
translations.idiomatic: Forty days after Shaoyang's death the Emperor still did not suspend court; he rotated commanders and reinforced the garrisons to await whatever came.

sentences.zh: 會傳言重質殺元濟，族其家，吉甫因請為少陽輟朝，遣使吊賻，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: It happened that rumor spread that Chongzhi had killed Yuanji and exterminated his clan; Jifu therefore requested that court be suspended for Shaoyang, that envoys be sent to condole and give burial gifts, and that [Shaoyang] be posthumously granted Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Then rumor ran that Chongzhi had killed Yuanji and wiped out his family; Jifu seized on it to ask for court mourning for Shaoyang, condolence envoys with burial gifts, and a posthumous grant of Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 而元濟不得命，乃悉兵四出，焚舞陽及葉，掠襄城、陽翟。

translations.literal: But Yuanji did not receive [imperial] appointment; he therefore deployed all his troops on four fronts, burning Wuyang and Ye, and plundering Xiangcheng and Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji received no appointment from the throne; he threw his whole army outward, burning Wuyang and Ye and ravaging Xiangcheng and Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 時許、汝居人皆竄伏榛莽間，剽系千餘里，關東大恐。

translations.literal: At the time the inhabitants of Xu and Ru all hid and crouched among brambles and thickets; plunder and capture extended more than a thousand li; the eastern passes were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: People in Xu and Ru hid in brush and thicket; raiding and capture ran for more than a thousand li, and the eastern heartland was gripped by fear.

sentences.zh: 吊使至，弗克入而還。

translations.literal: When the condolence envoys arrived, they could not enter and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The condolence mission reached the border but could not get in and turned back.

sentences.zh: 乃詔烏重胤兼汝州刺史，引軍壓其境，寧州刺史曹華為之副，以戍襄城；

translations.literal: An edict was then issued making Wu Chongyin also prefect of Ruzhou; he led troops to press their border; Cao Hua, prefect of Ningzhou, served as his deputy to garrison Xiangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Wu Chongyin to serve also as prefect of Ru and march his army to the frontier; Cao Hua of Ning served as his deputy and held Xiangcheng;

sentences.zh: 李光顏為忠武節度使，總兵臨屯；

translations.literal: Li Guangyan was made military commissioner of Zhongwu and gathered troops in encampment;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan was made military commissioner of Zhongwu and massed his army in camp;

sentences.zh: 析山南東道，詔節度使嚴綬為申、光、蔡等州招撫使，以中人崔潭峻監其軍。

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit was subdivided; an edict made the military commissioner Yan Shou pacification commissioner for Shen, Guang, Cai, and other prefectures, with the palace eunuch Cui Tanjun to oversee his army.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan East was split off; Yan Shou was named pacification commissioner for Shen, Guang, Cai, and the rest, with the eunuch Cui Tanjun to supervise his army.

sentences.zh: 下詔奪元濟官爵，趣諸道進討。

translations.literal: An edict was issued stripping Yuanji of office and rank and urging all circuits to advance in punitive attack.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Yuanji of rank and title and ordered every circuit to march against him.

sentences.zh: 時大旱，詔既下，雨雪凡三日。

translations.literal: At the time there was great drought; once the edict was issued, rain and snow fell for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: There was a severe drought; when the edict went out, rain and snow fell for three days.

sentences.zh: 田弘正、韓弘各遣子率兵隸綬、光顏軍。

translations.literal: Tian Hongzheng and Han Hong each sent their sons leading troops to serve under Yan Shou's and Li Guangyan's armies.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng and Han Hong each sent a son with troops to join Yan Shou's and Li Guangyan's commands.

sentences.zh: 綬屯蔡西鄙，師小勝，不設備，為賊襲，敗於礠丘，退保唐州。

translations.literal: Shou encamped on Cai's western border; his army won a small victory, made no preparations, was surprised by the rebels, defeated at Qiuqiu, and withdrew to hold Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shou camped on Cai's western frontier; after a minor victory he left his guard down, was hit by a rebel raid, routed at Qiuqiu, and fell back to Tang.

sentences.zh: 壽州刺史令狐通戰數北，賊乃拔霍丘，屠馬塘，通嬰城不敢出。

translations.literal: Linghu Tong, prefect of Shouzhou, fought and repeatedly retreated; the rebels then took Huoqiu, slaughtered Matang, and Tong clung to the city and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tong of Shou fought and lost again and again; the rebels took Huoqiu, massacred Matang, and Tong shut himself in the city and would not stir.

sentences.zh: 詔左金吾衛大將軍李文通宣慰，度其至，使代通。

translations.literal: An edict [named] Li Wentong, Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, as consolation commissioner; estimating when he would arrive, [the court] had him replace Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wentong, Grand General of the Left Golden Guard, was sent as consolation commissioner; the court timed his arrival so he could replace Tong.

sentences.zh: 會裴度輔政，賊始懼，而元濟不能有所指授，諸將趙昌、淩朝江、董重質、李祐、李憲、王覽、趙曄、王仁清等以便宜人自為戰，抗王師，有少誠、少陽舊風。

translations.literal: When Pei Du entered the government, the rebels first grew afraid; yet Yuanji could give no unified direction; the generals Zhao Chang, Ling Chaojiang, Dong Chongzhi, Li You, Li Xian, Wang Lan, Zhao Ye, Wang Renqing, and others fought each on his own authority as opportunity allowed, resisting the imperial armies with the old ways of Shaocheng and Shaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du joined the government the rebels began to fear; but Yuanji could not command them, and Zhao Chang, Ling Chaojiang, Dong Chongzhi, Li You, Li Xian, Wang Lan, Zhao Ye, Wang Renqing, and the rest fought on their own initiative, holding off the imperial armies in the old Shaocheng-Shaoyang style.

sentences.zh: 而李師道饋鹽，出入寧陵、雍丘間，韓弘知而不肯禁。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Li Shidao supplied salt, coming and going between Ningling and Yongqiu; Han Hong knew of it but would not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao meanwhile moved salt through Ningling and Yongqiu; Han Hong knew and would not stop it.

sentences.zh: 文通引兵與賊將王覽、董重質戰史蔟岡，馘覽首。

translations.literal: Wentong led troops against the rebel generals Wang Lan and Dong Chongzhi at Shicuo Ridge and took Wang Lan's head.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong met the rebel generals Wang Lan and Dong Chongzhi at Shicuo Ridge and took Wang Lan's head.

sentences.zh: 光顏又大破賊於時曲，復與重胤合擊賊小溵河，敗之，夷其屯塹。

translations.literal: Guangyan again routed the rebels at Shiqu, then joined Chongyin to strike the rebels at the Xiao River of Yin, defeated them, and leveled their camps and trenches.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan routed them again at Shiqu, then with Chongyin crushed them on the Little Yin River and tore down their camps and trenches.

sentences.zh: 天子責綬失律，更以韓弘兼都統，擢高霞寓唐、鄧、隨節度使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven blamed Shou for breach of discipline, replaced him by making Han Hong also overall commander, and promoted Gao Xiayu to military commissioner of Tang, Deng, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor blamed Shou for indiscipline, put Han Hong in overall command in his place, and promoted Gao Xiayu to military commissioner of Tang, Deng, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 十一年，諸軍大合。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the various armies massed together.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the allied armies gathered in force.

sentences.zh: 光顏壁掌河；

translations.literal: Guangyan fortified at Zhanghe;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan fortified at Zhanghe;

sentences.zh: 文通敗賊於固始，拔𨫼山；

translations.literal: Wentong defeated the rebels at Gushi and took Qie Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Wentong beat the rebels at Gushi and took Qie Mountain;

sentences.zh: 霞寓戰郎山，斬首千餘級，焚其壁，次鐵城。

translations.literal: Xiayu fought at Langshan, cut off more than a thousand heads, burned their ramparts, and advanced to Tiecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu fought at Lang Mountain, took more than a thousand heads, burned the rebel walls, and pushed on to Iron Fort.

sentences.zh: 賊偽奔，霞寓窮追，伏發，死傷略盡，退保新興，賊圍之，監軍李議誠馳入唐州。

translations.literal: The rebels feigned flight; Xiayu pursued to the limit; ambush erupted; dead and wounded were nearly all; he withdrew to hold Xinxing; the rebels besieged him; the army supervisor Li Yicheng galloped into Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels feigned retreat; Xiayu chased them to the end and walked into an ambush; his force was nearly wiped out; he fell back to Xinxing and was besieged, and the army supervisor Li Yicheng raced into Tang.

sentences.zh: 以救兵至，圍解，還守唐州。

translations.literal: When relief troops arrived, the siege was lifted; he returned to hold Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Relief arrived, the siege lifted, and he withdrew again to hold Tang.

sentences.zh: 元濟以霞寓敗，不足虞，並兵以備陳。

translations.literal: Yuanji, because Xiayu had been defeated, deemed [the threat] not worth worrying about and combined troops to guard against Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji, thinking Xiayu no longer mattered after his defeat, massed his troops to face Chen.

sentences.zh: 其秋，文通以兵銜枚夜出九女原，屠保壁三十所，分兵西北並安陽山，破屯邏數百人，降者萬餘，執兩將。

translations.literal: That autumn, Wentong led troops with gags in their mouths by night out of Jiunü Plain, slaughtered thirty garrison forts, divided troops northwest along Anyang Mountain, broke encampments numbering several hundred in succession, received more than ten thousand surrenders, and captured two generals.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Wentong marched his men gagged by night from Jiunü Plain, overran thirty garrison forts, sent columns northwest along Anyang Mountain, smashed one camp after another by the hundreds, accepted more than ten thousand surrenders, and took two generals.

sentences.zh: 光顏敗郾城兵二萬，俘六將，復與重胤合攻淩雲柵，拔之。

translations.literal: Guangyan defeated twenty thousand Yancheng troops, captured six generals, again joined Chongyin to attack the Lingyun stockade, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan routed twenty thousand men at Yancheng, took six generals, then with Chongyin stormed the Lingyun stockade and carried it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒諸軍無大功，詔內常侍梁守謙宣慰，因督戰，付詔書五百以待有功，斥金帛募死士。

translations.literal: The Emperor, angry that the armies had won no great victory, ordered the palace attendant Liang Shouqian as consolation commissioner and to supervise battle; he entrusted five hundred edicts to await those with merit and spent gold and silk to recruit death-defying warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that no army had won a decisive victory, the Emperor sent the palace attendant Liang Shouqian to supervise the campaign, with five hundred edicts ready to reward merit and gold and silk to recruit men willing to die.

sentences.zh: 進拜光顏檢校尚書左僕射，重胤右僕射，布御史中丞，公武御史大夫。

translations.literal: Guangyan was promoted and invested as Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Chongyin as Right Vice Director; Bu as Censor-in-Chief; Gongwu as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan was promoted to Acting Left Vice Director; Chongyin to Right Vice Director; Bu to Censor-in-Chief; and Gongwu to Chief Censor.

sentences.zh: 詔旨約束，厲賞罰，諸將恐懼。

translations.literal: Edict instructions imposed restraint; rewards and punishments were sharpened; the generals were fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders tightened discipline and sharpened rewards and punishments, and the generals were afraid.

sentences.zh: 貶霞寓，以袁滋代之。

translations.literal: Xiayu was demoted; Yuan Zi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayu was demoted and Yuan Zi took his place.

sentences.zh: 滋懦不能軍，更以李愬為唐、鄧、隨節度使。

translations.literal: Zi was timid and could not command an army; Li Su was again [appointed] military commissioner of Tang, Deng, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was too timid to lead an army, so Li Su was made military commissioner of Tang, Deng, and Sui instead.

sentences.zh: 元濟食盡，士卒食菱芡魚鱉皆竭，至斫草根以給者。

translations.literal: Yuanji's food was exhausted; the soldiers' water chestnuts, lotus seeds, fish, and turtles were all depleted, until they chopped roots and grass to supply themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji ran out of food; his men exhausted every water chestnut, lotus seed, fish, and turtle, until they were cutting roots and grass to eat.

sentences.zh: 民苦饑，相與四潰，元濟亦嗇其食，不復禁，諸將爭納之。

translations.literal: The people suffered famine and fled in all directions; Yuanji also stinted his food and no longer forbade [desertion]; the generals vied to take them in.
translations.idiomatic: The people starved and fled in every direction; Yuanji rationed his own stores, stopped trying to hold them back, and his generals competed to enlist the deserters.

sentences.zh: 帝始僑置郾城、吳房於行營，以綏新附。

translations.literal: The Emperor first provisionally placed Yancheng and Wufang at the field headquarters to pacify the newly attached.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor began lodging Yancheng and Wufang populations at the field headquarters to reassure the newly surrendered.

sentences.zh: 愬引兵攻其西，破屯柵十餘所，執丁士良、吳秀琳，皆賊票健者。

translations.literal: Su led troops to attack their west, broke more than ten stockade encampments, and captured Ding Shiliang and Wu Xiulin—both fierce stalwarts among the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Su struck their western line, overran more than a dozen stockades, and captured Ding Shiliang and Wu Xiulin, two of the rebels' fiercest fighters.

sentences.zh: 賊帥張伯良以兵三萬與光顏戰郾城，大敗。

translations.literal: The rebel commander Zhang Boliang led thirty thousand troops against Guangyan at Yancheng and was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commander Zhang Boliang brought thirty thousand men against Guangyan at Yancheng and was routed.

sentences.zh: 獲馬千匹、甲三萬首，伯良奔還蔡。

translations.literal: They captured a thousand horses and thirty thousand sets of armor; Boliang fled back to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: They took a thousand horses and thirty thousand suits of armor; Boliang fled back to Cai.

sentences.zh: 曹華取青陵城，斷郾歸路。

translations.literal: Cao Hua took Qingling city and cut the return route to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hua seized Qingling and severed the road back to Yan.

sentences.zh: 賊將鄧懷金懼，即送款，光顏受之。

translations.literal: The rebel general Deng Huaijin was afraid and at once submitted allegiance; Guangyan accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Deng Huaijin, in fear, offered surrender at once, and Guangyan accepted.

sentences.zh: 愬又襲破朗山，執戍將梁希果，平汶港等三壁。

translations.literal: Su again raided and broke Langshan, captured the garrison commander Liang Xiguo, and leveled the three forts of Wengang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Su raided Lang Mountain again, captured the garrison commander Liang Xiguo, and leveled Wengang and two other forts.

sentences.zh: 元濟知眾數潰，而外失秀琳等，因奉表請束身北闕下，帝遣使者許以不死。

translations.literal: Yuanji knew the masses were collapsing in flight and that he had lost Xiulin and others abroad; he therefore submitted a memorial asking to bind himself and come north beneath the palace gates; the Emperor sent envoys promising he would not die.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji saw his forces melting away and his best captains lost abroad; he memorialized asking to surrender himself at the northern palace gate, and the Emperor sent word that his life would be spared.

sentences.zh: 元濟取行營馬三百，董重質不與，故不果降。

translations.literal: Yuanji took three hundred horses from the field headquarters; Dong Chongzhi would not give them; therefore the surrender did not come off.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji tried to seize three hundred horses from the field camp; Chongzhi refused, and the surrender fell through.

sentences.zh: 訴略興橋，得守將李祐，不殺，引至帳下計議，始謀襲蔡，賊勢益沮。

translations.literal: Attacking the Xing Bridge outpost, he obtained the defending commander Li You; he did not kill him, but brought him to his tent for counsel; then he first plotted the raid on Cai, and rebel strength grew ever more dispirited.
translations.idiomatic: In a raid on the Xing Bridge garrison he captured its commander Li You, spared him, and brought him into his tent to plan; the scheme to strike Cai was born, and rebel morale sank further.

sentences.zh: 自少誠盜有蔡四十年，王師未嘗傅城下，又嘗敗韓全義、于頔，以是兵驕無所憚，內恃陂浸重阻，故合天下兵攻之，三年才克一二縣。

translations.literal: From the time Shaocheng stole possession of Cai for forty years, the imperial armies had never reached beneath the city walls; they had also once defeated Han Quanyi and Yu Di; for this reason the troops were arrogant and feared nothing; inwardly they relied on ponds, floods, and layered barriers—therefore though all the realm's armies attacked, in three years they took only one or two counties.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng had held Cai by force for forty years; imperial armies had never pressed the walls, and Han Quanyi and Yu Di had been beaten here; the garrison grew proud and fearless, trusting in moats, floods, and layered defenses—so even with all the empire's armies against them, three years brought only a county or two.

sentences.zh: 帝既責罷霞寓、滋等，諸將乃用命。

translations.literal: Once the Emperor had blamed and removed Xiayu, Zi, and others, the generals then obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor demoted Xiayu, Zi, and the rest, the generals at last took their orders.

sentences.zh: 詔起沙陀梟騎濟師，命裴度為彰義節度兼申、光、蔡四面行營招撫使。

translations.literal: An edict raised Shatuo elite cavalry to reinforce the army; Pei Du was ordered as military commissioner of Zhangyi and concurrently pacification commissioner of the four-sided field headquarters for Shen, Guang, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The court called up Shatuo shock cavalry as reinforcements and made Pei Du military commissioner of Zhangyi and pacification commissioner for the Shen-Guang-Cai field headquarters on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 梁守謙與諸將計，先度未至立功，諸將亟戰，不勝。

translations.literal: Liang Shouqian and the generals plotted that before Du arrived they should win merit; the generals fought repeatedly and did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shouqian and the generals agreed to win glory before Du arrived; they fought again and again and could not break through.

sentences.zh: 度至，大勞將士，皆感激請戰。

translations.literal: When Du arrived, he greatly rewarded officers and soldiers; all were moved and requested battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Du arrived he feasted and rewarded the troops; moved to gratitude, they all asked to fight.

sentences.zh: 間遣士入蔡，約元濟降，為左右所劫，不得降。

translations.literal: He secretly sent men into Cai to arrange Yuanji's surrender; they were coerced by those at his side, and he could not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men secretly into Cai to negotiate Yuanji's surrender, but Yuanji's inner circle blocked him and the surrender failed.

sentences.zh: 光顏每戰冠軍，故元濟悉眾亢時曲。

translations.literal: Guangyan every battle was first to win; therefore Yuanji deployed all his forces to resist at Shiqu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan won the first honors in every fight, so Yuanji massed his whole army to hold him at Shiqu.

sentences.zh: 祐為愬謀曰：「蔡之守者，市人疲卒耳，勁兵皆在外，若直搗縣瓠，賊成禽矣。」

translations.literal: You counseled Su, saying: "Cai's defenders are merely market-men and worn-out soldiers; the strong troops are all abroad; if one strikes straight at Xuanhu, the rebels will be captured whole."
translations.idiomatic: You advised Su, saying, "The men holding Cai are shopkeepers and spent soldiers; the crack troops are all abroad. Strike straight at Xuanhu and the rebels are yours."

sentences.zh: 愬然之，以精騎夜襲蔡，坎垣入之，戍者不知也。

translations.literal: Su agreed; with elite cavalry he raided Cai by night, entered through ramparts and ditches, and the garrison did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Su agreed; he took elite cavalry, raided Cai by night, crossed ditches and walls, and the garrison never knew.

sentences.zh: 賊恃董重質兵在洄曲，不虞師之至，及愬攻內城，防卒尚千餘接戰，元濟始驚，被甲乘城以待重質。

translations.literal: The rebels relied on Dong Chongzhi's troops being at Huaiqu and did not expect the army's arrival; when Su attacked the inner city, more than a thousand defending soldiers still joined battle; Yuanji first grew alarmed, donned armor, mounted the wall, and awaited Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels trusted Chongzhi's army at Huaiqu and never expected an attack; when Su hit the inner city more than a thousand defenders still fought; Yuanji woke in alarm, armored himself, and climbed the wall waiting for Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 會重贊降訴，而李進誠取賊庫兵，即攻之。

translations.literal: It happened that Chongzhi came forward in surrender; meanwhile Li Jincheng took the rebels' armory weapons and at once pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi chose that moment to surrender, while Li Jincheng seized the rebel armory and pressed the assault at once.

sentences.zh: 明日，燒其門，民相率抱薪增火，王師縱射，城上鏃可拾也。

translations.literal: The next day they burned the gates; the people one after another carried firewood to feed the flames; the imperial armies loosed arrows; on the wall bolts could be gathered up.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fired the gates; civilians rushed in with bundles of fuel; the imperial archers poured arrows until bolts littered the wall walk.

sentences.zh: 居二日，門壞，執元濟，舉族傳之長安。

translations.literal: After two days the gate was destroyed; Yuanji was captured; the whole clan was conveyed to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the gate gave way; Yuanji was taken, and his whole clan was sent to Chang'an in bonds.

sentences.zh: 申、光戍兵尚三萬，皆降。

translations.literal: The garrison troops of Shen and Guang still numbered thirty thousand; all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand garrison troops still held Shen and Guang; all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝禦興安門受俘，群臣稱賀，以元濟獻廟社，徇於市斬之，年二十五。

translations.literal: The Emperor proceeded to Xing'an Gate to receive the captive; the ministers offered congratulations; Yuanji was presented at the altars of soil and grain, displayed through the market and beheaded; he was twenty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received the captive at Xing'an Gate amid the ministers' congratulations; Yuanji was offered to the state altars, paraded through the market, and beheaded. He was twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 夜失其首。

translations.literal: By night his head was lost.
translations.idiomatic: That night his head disappeared.

sentences.zh: 妻沈沒入掖庭，二弟、三男子流江陵，皆殺之。

translations.literal: His wife Shen was confiscated into the Palace Reception; two younger brothers and three male children were exiled to Jiangling; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Shen was taken into the palace women's quarters; two younger brothers and three sons were exiled to Jiangling—and all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 斬其屬官劉協庶、趙曄、王仁清等十餘人。

translations.literal: His subordinate officials Liu Xiexu, Zhao Ye, Wang Renqing, and more than ten others were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of his officers, including Liu Xiexu, Zhao Ye, and Wang Renqing, were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 度還，以馬揔為留後，俄拜節度使，析溵州隸陳許。

translations.literal: When Du returned, he made Ma Cong acting commissioner; soon [Ma] was invested military commissioner; Yinzhou was split off and attached to Chenxu.
translations.idiomatic: When Du returned he left Ma Cong as acting commissioner; soon Ma was appointed military commissioner, and Yin Prefecture was carved out and placed under Chen-Xu.

sentences.zh: 始度之出，太子右庶子韓愈為行軍司馬，帝美度功，即命愈為《平淮西碑》，其文曰：

translations.literal: When Du first set out, Han Yu, Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, served as campaign marshal; the Emperor praised Du's merit and at once ordered Yu to compose the "Stele on the Pacification of Huai West"; its text says:
translations.idiomatic: When Du first marched out, Han Yu, Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, served as campaign marshal; the Emperor, admiring Du's achievement, ordered Yu to write the Stele on the Pacification of Huai West. Its text reads:

sentences.zh: 天以唐克肖其德，聖子神孫，繼繼承承，於千萬年，敬戒不怠，全付所覆，四海九州，罔有內外，悉主悉臣。

translations.literal: Heaven, because Tang matched its virtue, [granted] holy sons and divine grandsons, succeeding in unbroken succession for ten thousand years, reverent and vigilant without slackness, fully entrusting what was covered—within the four seas and nine provinces, none within or without, all lords all subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven matched Tang to its own virtue: holy sons and divine grandsons, line upon line, for ten thousand years—reverent, vigilant, never slack—entrusting the whole realm beneath its canopy; within the four seas and nine provinces, without distinction of inner and outer, every land a lord, every people a subject.

sentences.zh: 高祖、太宗，既除既治。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Taizong—both removed [obstacles] and governed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Taizong cleared away disorder and brought the realm to order.

sentences.zh: 高宗、中、睿，休養生息。

translations.literal: Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong—rested the people and nurtured life.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong let the people rest and recover.

sentences.zh: 至於玄宗，受報收功，極熾而豐，物眾地大，孽牙其間。

translations.literal: As for Xuanzong, he received recompense and gathered merit—most blazing and abundant; things were many and the land vast; evil sprouts grew among them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanzong the dynasty reaped its reward and gathered its harvest—glory at its height, wealth overflowing, a vast land and teeming goods—and evil took root in the midst of it all.

sentences.zh: 肅宗、代宗，德祖、順考，以勤以容。

translations.literal: Suzong and Daizong, Dezong and Shunzong as ancestors examined—by diligence and by forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong and Daizong, and the ancestral virtue of Dezong and Shunzong, met the age with diligence and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 大慝適去，莨莠不{𧂭}，相臣將臣，文恬武嬉，習熟見聞，以為當然。

translations.literal: The great villain had just gone; tares and weeds were not uprooted; chancellors and generals—civil men at ease, military men at play—grew accustomed in what they saw and heard and took it as natural.
translations.idiomatic: The great evil had only just departed, yet the tares were left unweeded; chancellors and commanders alike—scholars grown complacent, soldiers grown idle—came to accept what they saw and heard as the way things must be.

sentences.zh: 睿聖文武皇帝既受群臣朝，乃考圖數貢，曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: The Sage Civil and Military Emperor, having received the ministers' audience, then examined the charts and counted the tribute, and said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: The Sage Civil and Military Emperor, after receiving the court's homage, reviewed the maps and tallied the tribute, and said, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 天既全付予有家，今傳次在予，予不能事事，其何以見於郊廟！」

translations.literal: Heaven has fully entrusted to me my house; now the succession rests in me; if I cannot manage every affair, how shall I appear before the suburban altars and ancestral temple!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has entrusted the whole realm to my house, and now the succession is mine—if I cannot govern every matter well, how can I stand before the altars of Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple!"

sentences.zh: 群臣震懾走職。

translations.literal: The ministers, shaken in awe, went to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, awestruck, withdrew to their duties.

sentences.zh: 明年，平蜀。

translations.literal: The next year, [they] pacified Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 又明年，平江東。

translations.literal: The year after that again, [they] pacified Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, Jiangdong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 又明年，平澤潞，遂定易定，致魏、博、貝、衛、澶、相，無不從誌。

translations.literal: The year after that again, [they] pacified Ze and Lu, then settled Yi and Ding, brought Wei, Bo, Bei, Wei, Chan, and Xiang—all without failing to follow their will.
translations.idiomatic: Another year brought the pacification of Ze and Lu; Yi and Ding were secured, and Wei, Bo, Bei, Wei, Chan, and Xiang all submitted without exception.

sentences.zh: 皇帝曰：「不可究武，予其少息。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "One must not pursue warfare to the end; let me rest a little."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "We must not press war to the limit; I shall give it a brief rest."

sentences.zh: 九年，蔡將死，蔡人立其子元濟以請，不許，遂燒舞陽，犯葉、襄城，以動東都，放兵四劫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Cai commander died; the people of Cai installed his son Yuanji and petitioned [for recognition]; [the court] did not permit it; thereupon they burned Wuyang, attacked Ye and Xiangcheng to stir the Eastern Capital, and unleashed troops to plunder on every side.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Cai commander died; the people of Cai set up his son Yuanji and petitioned for court recognition. When the court refused, they burned Wuyang, struck Ye and Xiangcheng to threaten the Eastern Capital, and sent their soldiers raiding on every side.

sentences.zh: 皇帝歷問於朝，一二臣外，皆曰：「蔡帥之不廷授，於今五十年，傳三姓四將，其樹本堅，兵利卒頑，不與它等。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned throughout the court; apart from one or two ministers, all said: "The Cai commander's not being appointed by the court—for fifty years now, passed through three surnames and four generals; their roots are firm, weapons sharp, soldiers stubborn—not equal to the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor questioned the whole court; save for one or two ministers, all said, "The Cai commanders have gone fifty years without court appointment, passing through three clans and four generals. Their roots run deep, their arms are keen, their soldiers are hardened—unlike any other such power.

sentences.zh: 因撫而有，順且無事。」

translations.literal: By nurturing and possessing them, [they are] compliant and without trouble."
translations.idiomatic: If we soothe them and keep them, they will stay compliant and give no trouble."

sentences.zh: 大官臆決唱聲，萬口和附，並為一談，牢不可破。

translations.literal: High officials made presumptuous decisions, chanting in chorus; ten thousand mouths harmonized; all became one talk, firmly unbreakable.
translations.idiomatic: High officials made presumptuous pronouncements in chorus; ten thousand voices chimed in until one opinion prevailed, fixed and unbreakable.

sentences.zh: 皇帝曰：「惟天惟祖宗所以付任予者，庶其在此，予何敢不力！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Only Heaven and only the ancestors' reason for entrusting me—perhaps it lies herein; how dare I not exert myself!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What Heaven and the ancestors entrusted to me may well depend on this—how dare I fail to give my utmost!

sentences.zh: 況一二臣同，不為無助。」

translations.literal: Moreover one or two ministers agree—not without aid."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, one or two ministers stand with me—I am not without support."

sentences.zh: 曰：「光顏，汝為陳許帥，維是河東、魏博、郃陽三軍之在行者，汝皆將之。」

translations.literal: He said: "Guangyan, you are commander of Chen-Xu; as for the three armies of Hedong, Weibo, and Heyang that are in the field—you shall command them all."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Guangyan, you command Chen-Xu; all three field armies of Hedong, Weibo, and Heyang shall be under your command."

sentences.zh: 曰：「重胤，汝故有河陽、懷，今益以汝，維是朔方、義成、陜、益、鳳翔、鄜延、寧慶七軍之在行者，汝皆將之。」

translations.literal: He said: "Chongyin, you formerly held Heyang and Huai; now this is added to you; as for the seven armies of Shuofang, Yicheng, Shan, Yi, Fengxiang, Fuyan, and Ningqing that are in the field—you shall command them all."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Chongyin, you already hold Heyang and Huai; this charge is now added to you. All seven field armies of Shuofang, Yicheng, Shan, Yi, Fengxiang, Fuyan, and Ningqing shall be under your command."

sentences.zh: 曰：「弘，汝以卒萬二千屬而子公武往討之。」

translations.literal: He said: "Hong, you shall attach twelve thousand troops and send your son Gongwu to attack them."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Hong, detach twelve thousand troops and send your son Gongwu to chastise them."

sentences.zh: 曰：「文通，汝守壽，維是宣武、淮南、宣歙、浙西、徐泗五軍之行於壽者，汝皆將之。」

translations.literal: He said: "Wentong, you guard Shou; as for the five armies of Xuanwu, Huainan, Xuan-Xi, Zhexi, and Xu-Si operating at Shou—you shall command them all."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Wentong, you hold Shou; all five armies of Xuanwu, Huainan, Xuan-Xi, Zhexi, and Xu-Si operating there shall be under your command."

sentences.zh: 曰：「道古，汝其觀察鄂嶽。」

translations.literal: He said: "Daogu, you shall serve as inspector of E-Yue."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Daogu, you shall serve as inspector of E-Yue."

sentences.zh: 曰：「愬，汝帥唐、鄧、隨，各以其兵進戰。」

translations.literal: He said: "Su, you command Tang, Deng, and Sui; each with their troops shall advance to battle."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Su, you command Tang, Deng, and Sui; each shall advance to battle with its own forces."

sentences.zh: 曰：「度，汝長御史，其往視師。」

translations.literal: He said: "Du, you head the Censorate—go oversee the army."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Du, as head of the Censorate, go and oversee the army."

sentences.zh: 曰：「度，惟汝予同，汝遂相予，以賞罰用命不用命。」

translations.literal: He said: "Du, only you and I are one—you shall assist me, using reward and punishment for obedience and disobedience."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Du, you and I are as one—you shall serve as my chancellor, rewarding obedience and punishing disobedience."

sentences.zh: 曰：「弘，汝其以節都統諸軍。」

translations.literal: He said: "Hong, you shall with insignia of command serve as supreme commander of all armies."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Hong, you shall bear the insignia of command and serve as supreme commander of all armies."

sentences.zh: 曰：「守謙，汝出入左右，汝惟近臣，其往撫師。」

translations.literal: He said: "Shouqian, you attend me at court; as my close minister, go comfort the army."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Shouqian, you attend me in court; as my close minister, go and hearten the army."

sentences.zh: 曰：「度，汝其往，衣服飲食予士，無寒無饑，以既厥事，遂生蔡人。

translations.literal: He said: "Du, go; give clothing and food to the soldiers—none cold, none hungry—to complete the task and give life to the people of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Du, go. Clothe and feed the troops—let none suffer cold or hunger—finish the task, and spare the people of Cai.

sentences.zh: 賜汝節斧、通天禦帶、衛卒三百。

translations.literal: [I] grant you insignia-axe, heaven-piercing imperial belt, and three hundred guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: I grant you the insignia-axe, the heaven-piercing imperial belt, and three hundred guard soldiers.

sentences.zh: 凡茲廷臣，汝擇自從，惟其賢能，無憚大吏。

translations.literal: Of all these court ministers, you may choose whom to follow—only the worthy and capable—fear not great officials.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the ministers at court, choose whom you will to accompany you—only the worthy and capable—and do not fear high officials.

sentences.zh: 庚申，予其臨門送汝。」

translations.literal: On gengshen, I shall come to the gate to send you off."
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengshen I shall come to the gate to see you off."

sentences.zh: 曰：「御史，予閔士大夫戰甚苦，自今以往，非郊廟祀，無用樂。」

translations.literal: He said: "Censor, I pity that scholar-officials and soldiers fight in great hardship; from now on, except for suburban and temple sacrifices, no music shall be used."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Censor, I grieve that our officers and soldiers suffer so in battle. From this day forward, save for suburban and temple rites, no music shall be played."

sentences.zh: 顏、胤、武合攻其北，大戰十六，得柵城縣二十三，降人卒四萬。

translations.literal: Yan, Yin, and Wu jointly attacked the north; sixteen great battles; captured twenty-three stockade counties; surrendered people and soldiers forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan, Chongyin, and Gongwu jointly attacked from the north, fought sixteen major battles, took twenty-three fortified counties, and accepted the surrender of forty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 道古攻其東南，八戰，降萬三千，再入申，破其外城。

translations.literal: Daogu attacked the southeast; eight battles; ten thousand three hundred surrendered; entered Shen twice; broke the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu attacked the southeast in eight battles, accepted thirteen thousand surrenders, twice entered Shen, and breached the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 文通戰其東，十餘遇，降萬三千。

translations.literal: Wentong fought the east; more than ten encounters; ten thousand three hundred surrendered.
