translations.idiomatic: Wentong fought in the east in more than ten engagements and accepted thirteen thousand surrenders.

sentences.zh: 愬入其西，得賊將，輒釋不殺，用其策，戰比有功。

translations.literal: Su entered the west; when he captured rebel generals, he always released them without killing; used their strategies; battles increasingly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Su pressed in from the west; whenever he captured rebel generals he spared them, took their counsel, and battle after battle won success.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，丞相度至師，都統弘責戰益急，顏、胤、武戰益用命。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, eighth month: Chancellor Du arrived at the army; supreme commander Hong pressed battles more urgently; Yan, Yin, and Wu fought with increasing obedience.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year Chancellor Du reached the army; supreme commander Hong pressed the fighting harder, and Guangyan, Chongyin, and Gongwu fought with redoubled zeal.

sentences.zh: 元濟盡並其眾洄曲以備。

translations.literal: Yuanji gathered all his forces at Huaiqu to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji massed all his forces at Huaiqu to make ready.

sentences.zh: 十月壬申，愬用所得賊將，自文城因天大雪疾馳百二十里，用夜半到蔡，破其門，取元濟以獻，盡得其屬人卒。

translations.literal: Tenth month, renshen: Su used a captured rebel general; from Wencheng, taking advantage of heaven's heavy snow, galloped one hundred twenty li; at midnight reached Cai; broke the gate; captured Yuanji to present; fully obtained all dependents and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the tenth month Su used a captured rebel general as guide; from Wencheng he raced a hundred and twenty li through heaven's heavy snow, reached Cai at midnight, broke the gate, seized Yuanji and presented him captive, and took all his followers and troops.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，丞相度入蔡，以皇帝命赦其人。

translations.literal: Xinsi: Chancellor Du entered Cai; by the Emperor's order pardoned the people.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Chancellor Du entered Cai and, by imperial command, pardoned the people.

sentences.zh: 淮西平，大饗賫功。

translations.literal: Huai West was pacified; a grand feast rewarded merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huai West was pacified, and a great feast rewarded the victors.

sentences.zh: 師還之日，因以其食賜蔡人。

translations.literal: On the day the army returned, thereupon bestowed its food on the people of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the army marched home, its provisions were given to the people of Cai.

sentences.zh: 凡蔡卒三萬五千，其不樂為兵願歸為農者十九，悉縱之。

translations.literal: In all Cai soldiers numbered thirty-five thousand; of those unwilling to be soldiers and wishing to return as farmers, nine-tenths—all were released.
translations.idiomatic: Of thirty-five thousand Cai soldiers in all, nine in ten who wished to lay down arms and return to farming were released.

sentences.zh: 斬元濟京師。

translations.literal: Yuanji was beheaded in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was beheaded in the capital.

sentences.zh: 冊功：弘加侍中；

translations.literal: Merit was enrolled: Hong was made Privy Counselor;
translations.idiomatic: Merit was recorded: Hong was made Privy Counselor;

sentences.zh: 愬為左僕射，帥山南東道；

translations.literal: Su was made Left Vice Director, commander of Shannan East Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Su was made Left Vice Director and commander of Shannan East Circuit;

sentences.zh: 顏、胤皆加司空；

translations.literal: Yan and Yin were both made Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan and Chongyin were both made Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 公武以散騎常侍帥鄜、坊、丹、延；

translations.literal: Gongwu, as Regular Attendant, commanded Fu, Fang, Dan, and Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Gongwu, as Regular Attendant, was made commander of Fu, Fang, Dan, and Yan;

sentences.zh: 道古進大夫；

translations.literal: Daogu was promoted to Grand Master;
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was promoted to Grand Master;

sentences.zh: 文通加散騎常侍；

translations.literal: Wentong was made Regular Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Wentong was made Regular Attendant;

sentences.zh: 丞相度朝京師，進封晉國公，進階金紫光祿大夫，以舊官相；

translations.literal: Chancellor Du attended the capital, was advanced to Duke of Jin, advanced in rank to Golden Signet and Purple Ray Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, and retained his former office as Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Du came to court, was enfeoffed Duke of Jin, raised to Golden Signet and Purple Ray Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, and continued as Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 而以其副揔為工部尚書，領蔡任。

translations.literal: And his deputy Cong was made Minister of Works, holding the Cai assignment.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Ma Cong was made Minister of Works and given charge of Cai.

sentences.zh: 既還奏，群臣請紀聖功，被之金石。

translations.literal: Having returned and reported, the ministers requested that the sacred merit be recorded and spread upon metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned and reported, the ministers asked that the sacred achievement be recorded and cut into metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 皇帝以命臣愈，愈再拜稽首而獻文曰：

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered his subject Yu; Yu twice bowed prostrate and presented the text, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor charged his subject Yu; Yu bowed twice to the ground and presented the text, saying:

sentences.zh: 唐承天命，遂臣萬方。

translations.literal: Tang received Heaven's mandate and then made the myriad regions subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Tang received Heaven's mandate and brought the myriad lands to submission.

sentences.zh: 孰居近土，襲盜以狂？

translations.literal: Who, dwelling in nearby lands, inherited robbery in madness?
translations.idiomatic: Who, dwelling on the near marches, took up brigandage in reckless pride?

sentences.zh: 往在玄宗，崇極而圮。

translations.literal: Formerly under Xuanzong, [the realm] reached the utmost height and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanzong of old the realm rose to its zenith—and then fell.

sentences.zh: 河北悍驕，河南附起。

translations.literal: Hebei was fierce and arrogant; Henan rose in attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei grew fierce and proud; Henan rose in its wake.

sentences.zh: 四聖不宥，屢興師征。

translations.literal: Four sage emperors showed no mercy; repeatedly raised armies to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Four sage emperors showed no indulgence and repeatedly raised armies to chastise them.

sentences.zh: 有不能克，益戍以兵。

translations.literal: Some could not be conquered; garrisons were increased with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Where they could not be subdued, garrisons were thickened with troops.

sentences.zh: 夫耕不食，婦織不裳。

translations.literal: Husbands plowed but did not eat; wives wove but had no garments.
translations.idiomatic: Husbands plowed yet had no grain to eat; wives wove yet had no cloth to wear.

sentences.zh: 輸之以車，為卒賜糧。

translations.literal: It was conveyed by cart to give soldiers grain.
translations.idiomatic: Cartloads were sent forth to feed the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 外多失朝，曠不嶽狩。

translations.literal: Outside [the capital] many missed court; vast intervals passed without mountain hunts.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the provinces missed court; long ages passed without an imperial hunt at the sacred peaks.

sentences.zh: 百隸怠官，事亡其舊。

translations.literal: The hundred officials slacked in office; affairs lost their former ways.
translations.idiomatic: Officials everywhere grew slack; government lost its old order.

sentences.zh: 帝時繼位，顧瞻咨嗟：「惟汝文武，孰恤予家？」

translations.literal: The Emperor then succeeded the throne, looked about and sighed: "Only you, civil and military—who will care for my house?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then took the throne, looked about, and sighed, "You civil and military servants—who will tend my house?"

sentences.zh: 既斬吳、蜀，旋取山東。

translations.literal: Having beheaded Wu and Shu, he then took Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Having cut down Wu and Shu, he turned and took Shandong.

sentences.zh: 魏將首義，六州降從。

translations.literal: The Wei general was first in righteousness; six prefectures surrendered and followed.
translations.idiomatic: A Weibo general led the way in loyalty; six prefectures submitted and followed.

sentences.zh: 淮蔡不順，自以為強。

translations.literal: Huai and Cai were not compliant; they thought themselves strong.
translations.idiomatic: Huai and Cai would not submit, deeming themselves strong.

sentences.zh: 提兵叫讙，欲事故常。

translations.literal: They raised troops, shouting and clamoring, wishing old affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: They raised troops, shouting in defiance, demanding the old ways restored.

sentences.zh: 始命討之，遂連奸鄰。

translations.literal: At first [the court] ordered them chastised; then they linked with wicked neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court ordered them punished; then they allied with treacherous neighbors.

sentences.zh: 陰遣刺客，來賊相臣。

translations.literal: Secretly they sent assassins to come and harm the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In secret they sent assassins to strike at the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 方戰未利，內驚京師。

translations.literal: Just as battle was not yet favorable, within [the realm] the capital was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: While the campaign still hung in the balance, alarm shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 群公上言：「莫若惠來。」

translations.literal: The group of lords submitted saying: "Better to show kindness and let them come."
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers submitted, saying, "Better to show mercy and accept their submission."

sentences.zh: 帝為不聞，與神為謀。

translations.literal: The Emperor acted as if he had not heard; he conspired with the divine.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor acted as though he had not heard and took counsel with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 及相同德，以訖天誅。

translations.literal: When the chancellor shared virtue, thereby Heaven's punishment was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When chancellor and throne stood as one in purpose, Heaven's judgment was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 乃敕顏、胤，愬、武、古、通：「鹹統於弘，各奏汝功。」

translations.literal: Then he decreed to Yan, Yin, Su, Wu, Gu, and Tong: "All uniformly under Hong—each report your merit."
translations.idiomatic: Then he decreed to Guangyan, Chongyin, Su, Gongwu, Daogu, and Wentong, "All shall be unified under Hong; each report your achievements."

sentences.zh: 三方分攻，五萬其師。

translations.literal: Three directions divided the attack; fifty thousand were their army.
translations.idiomatic: Three armies attacked from separate quarters; their force numbered fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 大兵北乘，厥數倍之。

translations.literal: The great army pressed north; that number was several times over.
translations.idiomatic: The main force pressed northward, several times that number strong.

sentences.zh: 嘗兵時曲，軍士蠢蠢。

translations.literal: Once they battled at Shiqu; the soldiers were muddled and uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: At Shiqu they once gave battle, and the troops grew restless and confused.

sentences.zh: 既翦淩雲，蔡卒大窘。

translations.literal: Having cut down Lingyun, the Cai soldiers were greatly cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lingyun was taken, the Cai troops were driven to desperation.

sentences.zh: 勝之邵陵，郾城來降。

translations.literal: Victory at Shaoling; Yancheng came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Victory at Shaoling; Yancheng surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自夏及秋，復屯相望。

translations.literal: From summer to autumn, camps faced each other again and again.
translations.idiomatic: From summer into autumn the camps faced one another across the lines.

sentences.zh: 兵頓不勵，告功不時。

translations.literal: The army stalled and was not stirred; merit was reported not in season.
translations.idiomatic: The army stalled without drive; reports of victory came late.

sentences.zh: 帝哀征夫，命相往厘。

translations.literal: The Emperor pitied the campaigners and ordered the chancellor to go and put things in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved for the men at war and sent the chancellor to set matters right.

sentences.zh: 士飽而歌，馬騰於槽。

translations.literal: Soldiers, sated, sang; horses leaped at the mangers.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers ate their fill and sang; horses stamped and frolicked at the troughs.

sentences.zh: 試之新城，賊遇敗逃。

translations.literal: Tested at Xincheng, the rebels met defeat and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tried at Xincheng, the rebels were broken and fled.

sentences.zh: 盡抽其有，聚以防我。

translations.literal: They fully drew what they had and gathered to defend against us.
translations.idiomatic: They stripped every resource and massed it to hold us off.

sentences.zh: 西師躍入，道無留者。

translations.literal: The western army leaped in; on the roads none remained.
translations.idiomatic: The western army surged in; on every road none dared stand in their way.

sentences.zh: 頟頟蔡城，其疆千里。

translations.literal: Towering was Cai city; its territory a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty stood the city of Cai, its domain a thousand li wide.

sentences.zh: 既入而有，莫不順俟。

translations.literal: Once entered and possessed, none failed to comply and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Once it was entered and taken, all submitted and awaited their fate.

sentences.zh: 帝有恩言，相度來宣：誅止其魁，釋於下人。

translations.literal: The Emperor had gracious words; Chancellor Du came to proclaim: punish only the ringleader; release the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor spoke in mercy; Chancellor Du came to proclaim: punish only the leaders, spare the common people.

sentences.zh: 蔡之卒夫，投甲呼舞。

translations.literal: Cai's soldier-farmers cast off armor and shouted in dance.
translations.idiomatic: Cai's fighting men cast off their armor and shouted for joy.

sentences.zh: 蔡之婦女，迎門笑語。

translations.literal: Cai's women greeted at the gates with laughter and talk.
translations.idiomatic: Cai's women came to their gates laughing and calling greetings.

sentences.zh: 蔡人告饑，船粟往哺。

translations.literal: The people of Cai reported hunger; boatloads of grain were sent to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Cai reported hunger, grain was shipped to feed them.

sentences.zh: 蔡人告寒，賜以繒布。

translations.literal: The people of Cai reported cold; silk cloth was bestowed on them.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Cai reported cold, silk and cloth were given them.

sentences.zh: 始時蔡人，禁不往來。

translations.literal: At first the people of Cai were forbidden to come and go.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people of Cai were forbidden to travel back and forth.

sentences.zh: 今相從戲，裏門夜開。

translations.literal: Now together at play, inner gates open by night.
translations.idiomatic: Now they stroll and play together, inner gates open through the night.

sentences.zh: 始時蔡人，進戰退戮。

translations.literal: At first the people of Cai—advance to battle, retreat to slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people of Cai advanced to battle and retreated to execution.

sentences.zh: 今眠而起，左餐右粥。

translations.literal: Now they sleep and rise; food on the left, porridge on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Now they sleep and wake to meals spread left and right, grain and porridge in plenty.

sentences.zh: 為之擇人，以收餘憊。

translations.literal: For them [the court] chose people to gather the remaining exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Men were chosen for them to gather up the weary and restore the land.

sentences.zh: 選吏賜牛，教而不稅。

translations.literal: Officials were selected, oxen bestowed; they were taught without taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were appointed, oxen were given, and they were taught farming without levy.

sentences.zh: 蔡人有言：「始迷不知，今乃大覺，羞前之為。」

translations.literal: The people of Cai have words: "At first confused and unknowing, now greatly awakened—ashamed of former deeds."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Cai said, "We were blind and did not know; now we are fully awakened and ashamed of what we did before."

sentences.zh: 蔡人有言：「天子明聖，不順族誅，順保性命。

translations.literal: The people of Cai have words: "The Son of Heaven is bright and sage; not compliant—the clan is executed; compliant—life is preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Cai said, "The Son of Heaven is wise and holy: resist, and your clan is destroyed; submit, and your lives are spared.

sentences.zh: 汝不吾信，視此蔡方。

translations.literal: You do not believe us—look at this Cai region.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not believe us, look at Cai itself.

sentences.zh: 孰為不順，往斧其吭。

translations.literal: Whoever is not compliant—go ax their throats.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever will not submit—go cut down his throat.

sentences.zh: 凡叛有數，聲勢相倚。

translations.literal: Generally rebels have their numbers; sound and might lean on each other.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels everywhere are counted by the score; each leans on another's strength and renown.

sentences.zh: 吾強不支，汝弱奚恃？

translations.literal: We are strong yet cannot sustain; you are weak—on what do you rely?
translations.idiomatic: We are mighty yet cannot endure; you are feeble—what do you trust?

sentences.zh: 其告而長，而父而兄；

translations.literal: Let them tell their elders, their fathers, their elder brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Let them go tell their elders, their fathers, and their elder brothers;

sentences.zh: 奔走來階，同我太平。」

translations.literal: Run hastening to our steps, sharing our great peace."
translations.idiomatic: Let them hurry to our threshold and share in our age of peace."

sentences.zh: 淮蔡為亂，天子伐子。

translations.literal: When Huai and Cai rebelled, the Son of Heaven chastised his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai and Cai rose in rebellion, the Son of Heaven marched against his rebellious subjects.

sentences.zh: 既伐而饑，天子活之。

translations.literal: Having conquered yet finding famine, the Son of Heaven kept them alive.
translations.idiomatic: Though the campaign had ended, famine followed; the Son of Heaven sustained the people.

sentences.zh: 始議伐蔡，卿士莫隨。

translations.literal: When first they debated attacking Cai, ministers and officials none followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first debated attacking Cai, not one minister or official would follow.

sentences.zh: 既伐四年，小大並疑。

translations.literal: Four years into the campaign, great and small alike doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Four years into the war, high and low alike were filled with doubt.

sentences.zh: 不赦不疑，由天子明。

translations.literal: Neither pardoning wrongly nor doubting wrongly—through the Son of Heaven's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: He neither pardoned the guilty nor doubted the loyal—such was the Son of Heaven's clarity.

sentences.zh: 凡此蔡功，惟斷乃成。

translations.literal: All this achievement at Cai was accomplished only through decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: All that was won at Cai was won only because he would not waver.

sentences.zh: 既定淮蔡，四夷畢來。

translations.literal: Once Huai and Cai were settled, all the four barbarians came.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huai and Cai were pacified, the peoples of the four quarters all came in submission.

sentences.zh: 遂開明堂，坐以治之。

translations.literal: Then the Bright Hall was opened, and he sat therein to govern.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Bright Hall was opened, and there he took his seat to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 愈以元濟之平，繇度能固天子意，得不赦，故諸將不敢首鼠，卒禽之，多歸度功，而愬特以入蔡功居第一。

translations.literal: Yu held that Yuanji's pacification came because Du could firm the Son of Heaven's resolve and obtain no amnesty, so the generals dared not waver, ultimately capturing him; many credited Du's merit, yet Su alone ranked first for entering Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu held that Wu Yuanji's defeat owed to Du Du's ability to fix the emperor's resolve and secure a policy of no pardon, so the generals dared not hang back, and Yuanji was taken at last. Many credited Du with the victory, but Li Su alone was ranked first for the exploit of entering Cai.

sentences.zh: 愬妻，唐安公主女也，出入禁中，訴愈文不實。

translations.literal: Su's wife was a daughter of Princess Tang'an; entering and leaving the inner palace, she complained that Yu's text was untrue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su's wife was the daughter of Princess Tang'an. Moving freely in and out of the inner palace, she complained that Han Yu's inscription did not tell the truth.

sentences.zh: 帝亦重牾武臣心，詔斫其文，更命翰林學士段文昌為之。

translations.literal: The emperor also valued not offending the martial lords' hearts; he decreed the text chiseled away and ordered Hanlin Academician Duan Wenchang to write a new one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also weighed the need not to alienate his military commanders. He ordered Han Yu's text cut from the stone and commanded the Hanlin Academician Duan Wenchang to compose another in its place.

sentences.zh: 李祐以功遷神武將軍，賜田宅米粟。

translations.literal: Li You, for merit, was transferred to General of Divine Martiality and granted fields, dwellings, rice, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Li You was promoted to General of the Divine Martial Guard for his service and was granted farmland, a residence, rice, and grain.

sentences.zh: 帝跡董重質教元濟亂，欲誅之，而李愬先許不死，故貶春州司戶參軍；

translations.literal: The emperor traced Dong Chongzhi's teaching Yuanji rebellion and wished to execute him, but Li Su had earlier promised he would not die, so he was demoted to registrar of Spring Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traced Dong Chongzhi's role in teaching Wu Yuanji rebellion and wished to put him to death, but Li Su had already promised he would not die, so Dong was demoted to registrar of Spring Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 淩朝江潘州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Ling Chaojiang [was demoted to] registrar of Pan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Chaojiang was demoted to registrar of Pan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲，申、蔡州始輸貢物，戶部以其久不至，請元日陳於廷。

translations.literal: That year Shen and Cai prefectures first submitted tribute goods; the Household Ministry, because they had long not arrived, requested they be displayed at court on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shen and Cai prefectures submitted tribute goods for the first time. Because they had long been absent from court, the Ministry of Revenue asked that they be displayed in the hall on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 祐字慶之，後擢夏、綏、銀、宥節度使，徙涇原。

translations.literal: You, styled Qingzhi, was later promoted to commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You circuits and transferred to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li You, styled Qingzhi, was later made military commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You and then transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 討李同捷也，改滄德景節度，累檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Li Tongjie, he was changed to Cangdejing commissioner and rose to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Li Tongjie he was made commissioner of Cangde and Jing and eventually rose to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 重質之貶，未幾，轉太子少詹事，隸武寧軍，遷左神武將軍，賫金幣與功臣等。

translations.literal: Not long after Chongzhi's demotion, he was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, attached to the Wuning army, promoted to Left General of Divine Martiality, and granted gold and coins equal to the meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after his demotion, Dong Chongzhi was made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, attached to the Wuning army, then promoted to Left General of the Divine Martial Guard and granted gold and coin equal to the other meritorious officers.

sentences.zh: 擢累左右神策劍南西川行營節度使，歷帥夏、綏、銀、宥，訓兵有法，羌、戎畏服。

translations.literal: He was promoted through Left and Right Shence and Jiannan Xichuan campaign commissioner, successively commanding Xia, Sui, Yin, and You; he trained troops with method, and the Qiang and Rong feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts as commander of the Left and Right Shence armies and campaign commissioner of Jiannan West, and successively governed Xia, Sui, Yin, and You. He drilled his troops with discipline, and the Qiang and Rong both feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 終右龍武統軍，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He ended as commander of the Right Dragon Martial army and was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard and was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉悟，其祖正臣，平盧軍節度使，襲范陽不克，死。

translations.literal: Liu Wu—his grandfather Zhengchen was Pinglu army commissioner, attacked Fanyang without success, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu's grandfather Liu Zhengchen had been military commissioner of Pinglu. He attacked Fanyang without success and died in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 叔父全諒，節度宣武，器其敢毅，署牙將，以罪奔潞州。

translations.literal: His uncle Quanliang, commissioner of Xuanwu, valued his boldness and resolution, appointed him a yamen general; for a crime he fled to Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Liu Quanliang, military commissioner of Xuanwu, admired his boldness and appointed him a yamen general. Later, after committing a crime, Wu fled to Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王虔休復署為將，被病去，還東都，全諒積緡錢數百萬在焉，悟破滕鐍用之。

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu again appointed him a general; he fell ill and left, returned to the eastern capital, and Quanliang had accumulated millions in cash there—Wu broke the lock and used it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu again appointed him as a general, but Wu fell ill and resigned. When he returned to the eastern capital, he found that Quanliang had left several million strings of cash there. Wu broke the lock and spent it.

sentences.zh: 從惡少年殺人屠狗，豪橫犯法，系河南獄，留守韋夏卿貸免。

translations.literal: He followed bad youths in killing people and butchering dogs, domineering and breaking the law; he was imprisoned in Henan jail, and garrison commander Wei Xiaqing pardoned and released him.
translations.idiomatic: He ran with violent young men, killing people and butchering dogs, swaggering and breaking the law until he was jailed in Henan. The garrison commander Wei Xiaqing secured his release.

sentences.zh: 李師古厚幣迎之，始未甚知，後從擊球，軒然馳突，撞師古馬仆，師古恚，將斬之，悟盛氣以語觸師古，不慴，師古奇其才，令將後軍，妻以從胃，歷牙門右職。

translations.literal: Li Shigu welcomed him with generous gifts; at first he did not know him well. Later, while playing cuju, Wu rode boldly charging, knocked Shigu's horse down; Shigu was angry and was about to execute him. Wu spoke with fierce spirit and offended Shigu, yet did not fear. Shigu admired his talent, made him lead the rear army, married him to Congwei, and he rose through senior yamen posts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu welcomed him with rich gifts. At first Shigu did not think much of him, but once, during a cuju match, Wu charged forward on horseback and knocked Shigu from his mount. Shigu flew into a rage and was about to have him executed, but Wu answered back with fierce defiance and showed no fear. Shigu came to admire his talent, put him in command of the rear guard, married him to a woman of the Congwei clan, and gradually raised him to senior posts in the yamen.

sentences.zh: 師道以軍用屈，率賈人錢為助，命悟督之。

translations.literal: Shidao, with military funds strained, collected merchants' money as aid and ordered Wu to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: When military funds ran short, Li Shidao levied money from the merchants for the war effort and put Wu in charge of collecting it.

sentences.zh: 悟獨寬假，人皆歸賴。

translations.literal: Wu alone was lenient, and people all relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu alone showed leniency, and the people came to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 師道被討，使將兵屯曹，法一而信，士卒樂為用，軍中刁鬥不鳴。

translations.literal: When Shidao came under attack, he sent Wu to garrison Cao with uniform law and trust; the soldiers were glad to serve, and no alarm signals sounded in the camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao came under imperial attack, Wu was sent to garrison Cao. His discipline was strict and fair, his word was trusted, and the soldiers served him willingly; not once did the camp alarms sound.

sentences.zh: 田弘正兵屯陽谷，悟徙營潭趙，魏師逾河取盧縣，壁阿井，城中飛語以謂馮利涉與悟當為帥。

translations.literal: Tian Hongzheng's troops garrisoned Yanggu; Wu moved camp to Tan and Zhao. Wei troops crossed the river, took Lu County, and walled at Aijing. Rumors flew in the city that Feng Lishe and Wu ought to be commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng's army encamped at Yanggu while Wu shifted his camp to Tan and Zhao. Wei troops crossed the Yellow River, took Lu County, and fortified at Aijing. Rumors swept the city that Feng Lishe and Liu Wu should be made commanders.

sentences.zh: 師道內疑，數召悟計事，悟曰：「今與魏如角力者，勢已交，先退者負。

translations.literal: Shidao inwardly suspicious, repeatedly summoned Wu to counsel. Wu said: "Now with Wei it is like wrestlers—their forces already engaged; whoever retreats first loses.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao grew inwardly suspicious and repeatedly summoned Wu for counsel. Wu said, "We and Wei are like wrestlers locked together: the contest is already joined, and whoever pulls back first loses.

sentences.zh: 悟還，魏踵薄城下矣。」

translations.literal: If Wu withdraws, Wei will follow pressing to the city walls."
translations.idiomatic: If I withdraw, Wei will press straight to the walls."

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰：「兵成敗未可知，殺大將，孰肯為用？」

translations.literal: His attendants remonstrated: "The battle's outcome is not yet known—kill a great general, and who will serve?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants remonstrated, "The outcome of battle is still uncertain. Kill a great general, and who will fight for you?"

sentences.zh: 師道然之。

translations.literal: Shidao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao agreed with them.

sentences.zh: 或言悟且亂，不如速去，師道遣使兩輩來責戰，密語其副張暹使斬悟。

translations.literal: Some said Wu was about to rebel and that it would be better to leave quickly. Shidao sent two sets of envoys to demand battle and secretly told his deputy Zhang Xian to kill Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Wu was about to mutiny and that Shidao had best leave at once. Shidao sent two sets of envoys to demand that Wu attack, while secretly instructing his deputy Zhang Xian to kill him.

sentences.zh: 使者與暹屏語移時，悟疑之，暹以情告，悟乃斬使者，召諸將議曰：「魏博兵強，出則敗，不出則死。

translations.literal: The envoys and Xian spoke in private for a long time; Wu grew suspicious. Xian told him the truth, and Wu then killed the envoys. He summoned the generals and said: "Wei-Bo troops are strong—go out and be defeated; stay in and die.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys spoke with Zhang Xian in private for a long while. Wu grew suspicious, and Xian told him the whole plot. Wu then killed the envoys, summoned the generals, and said, "Weibo's troops are strong. If we go out, we are defeated; if we stay in, we die.

sentences.zh: 且天子所誅，司空而已。

translations.literal: Besides, what the Son of Heaven punishes is the Minister alone.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Son of Heaven seeks only to punish the Minister himself.

sentences.zh: 吾屬為驅迫就死地，孰若還兵取鄆立大功，轉危亡為富貴乎？」

translations.literal: We are driven to certain death—is it not better to turn the army, take Yan, achieve great merit, and transform peril into riches and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: We are being driven to our deaths. Would it not be better to turn the army, seize Yan, win a great victory, and turn peril into wealth and honor?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆唯唯，而別將趙垂棘沮其行，悟因殺之，並殺所惡三十人，屍帳前，眾畏伏。

translations.literal: All murmured agreement, but subordinate general Zhao Chuiji discouraged the plan, so Wu killed him, also killed thirty he hated, corpses before the tent—the crowd feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: All murmured agreement, but the subordinate general Zhao Chuiji tried to stop them. Wu killed him, then killed thirty others he hated and laid their corpses before the tent. The army was cowed into submission.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「入鄆，人賞錢十萬，聽復私怨，財畜恣取之，唯完軍帑，違者斬。」

translations.literal: He ordered: "Enter Yan—each man rewarded one hundred thousand cash, allowed to settle private grudges, property and livestock taken freely; only preserve military stores—violators executed."
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "When we enter Yan, each man shall receive one hundred thousand cash. Private scores may be settled, and goods and livestock may be taken freely—only the army stores must remain intact. Violators will be executed."

sentences.zh: 因遣報弘正，使進兵潭趙。

translations.literal: He then sent word to Hongzheng to advance troops to Tan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent word to Tian Hongzheng asking him to advance on Tan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 悟夜半薄西門，黎明啟而入，殺師道並大將魏銑等數十人。

translations.literal: At midnight Wu pressed the west gate; at dawn the gates opened and he entered, killing Shidao along with great generals Wei Xian and others, several dozen in all.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Wu pressed the west gate. At dawn the gates were opened to him, and he entered and killed Li Shidao together with the great generals Wei Xian and several dozen others.

sentences.zh: 即拜悟義成節度使，封彭城郡王，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: Wu was immediately appointed Yicheng commissioner, enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng Commandery, with five hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was immediately appointed military commissioner of Yicheng, enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng Commandery with five hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年來朝，進檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe he came to court and was promoted to acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe he came to court and was promoted to acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，徙昭義軍。

translations.literal: When Muzong was enthroned, Wu was transferred to the Zhaoyi army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Wu was transferred to command the Zhaoyi army.

sentences.zh: 朱克融亂，議者假威名以厭其亂，移守盧龍。

translations.literal: Zhu Kerong rebelled; debaters borrowed Wu's fame to quell the chaos and moved him to guard Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Kerong rebelled, court advisers hoped Wu's reputation alone would suppress the disorder and transferred him to guard Lulong.

sentences.zh: 至邢州，會王廷湊之變，不得入，還屯。

translations.literal: Reaching Xing Prefecture, he met Wang Tingcou's mutiny, could not enter, and returned to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xing Prefecture, Wang Tingcou's mutiny broke out. Unable to enter, he withdrew and encamped where he was.

sentences.zh: 進兼幽、鎮招討使，治邢州。

translations.literal: He was promoted concurrently to You and Zhen pacification commissioner and governed Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent pacification commissioner of You and Zhen and governed from Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 圍臨城，觀望久不拔，與監軍劉承偕不葉，眾辱悟，縱其下亂法，悟不堪其忍。

translations.literal: Besieging Lincheng, he watched long without taking it; incompatible with supervisor Liu Chengxie, the troops insulted Wu and let subordinates break discipline—Wu could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Lincheng but lingered without taking it. He clashed with the army supervisor Liu Chengxie, and his troops humiliated Wu while letting their subordinates break discipline until Wu could bear it no longer.

sentences.zh: 承偕與都將張問謀縛悟送京師，以問代節度事。

translations.literal: Chengxie and chief general Zhang Wen plotted to bind Wu and send him to the capital, with Wen to replace him as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxie and the chief general Zhang Wen plotted to bind Wu and send him to the capital, with Zhang Wen to take over the command.

sentences.zh: 悟知之，以兵圍監軍，殺小使。

translations.literal: Wu learned of it, surrounded the supervisor with troops, and killed junior envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu learned of the plot, he surrounded the supervisor with troops and killed several of his attendants.

sentences.zh: 其屬賈直言質責悟曰：「李司空死有知，使公所為至此，軍中將復有如公者矣！」

translations.literal: His subordinate Jia Zhiyan reproached Wu, saying: "If Minister Li were conscious in death and saw your conduct reach this point, there will again be men like you in the army!"
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Jia Zhiyan rebuked him, saying, "If the late Minister Li could see from the grave what you have done, the army will produce more men just like you!"

sentences.zh: 悟遽謝曰：「吾不欲聞李司空字，少選當定。」

translations.literal: Wu hurriedly apologized: "I do not wish to hear the name Minister Li—a little while and it will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Wu hastily apologized, "I do not want to hear the name of Minister Li mentioned again. In a little while all will be settled."

sentences.zh: 即撝兵退，匿承偕囚之。

translations.literal: He immediately withdrew the troops, hid Chengxie, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately withdrew his troops, hid Chengxie, and kept him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 帝重違其心，貶承偕，然悟自是頗專肆，上書言多不恭。

translations.literal: The emperor, loath to oppose his will, demoted Chengxie; yet from then Wu was quite arbitrary, and his memorials were often disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, unwilling to defy him, demoted Chengxie instead. From then on Wu grew increasingly high-handed, and his memorials to the throne were often insolent.

sentences.zh: 天下負罪亡命者多歸之，強列其冤。

translations.literal: Fugitives with crimes throughout the realm many joined him, forcefully listing their grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals and fugitives from across the empire flocked to him, pressing their grievances upon him by force of numbers.

sentences.zh: 累進檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was accumulated promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，巫者妄言師道以兵屯鎦璃陂，悟惶恐，命禱祭，具千人膳，自往求哀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli, shamans falsely said Shidao's ghost was garrisoning troops at the Liuli embankment. Wu was terrified, ordered prayers and sacrifices, prepared a feast for a thousand, and went himself to plead.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoli reign, shamans falsely claimed that Li Shidao's ghost was encamped with an army at the Liuli embankment. Terrified, Wu ordered prayers and sacrifices, prepared a feast for a thousand men, and went in person to plead for mercy.

sentences.zh: 將易衣，嘔血數鬥，卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: About to change clothes, he vomited blood by the dou and died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to change clothes, he vomited several dou of blood and died. He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 表其子從諫嗣。

translations.literal: He memorialized that his son Congjian should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne asking that his son Li Congjian succeed him.

sentences.zh: 從諫，母微賤，少狡獪。

translations.literal: Congjian—his mother was of humble origin; in youth he was cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congjian's mother came from a humble background, and in youth he was shrewd and slippery.

sentences.zh: 師道時，使悟出屯，署從諫門下別奏。

translations.literal: During Shidao's time, Wu was sent to garrison abroad and appointed Congjian as memorial secretary under the gate.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Shidao still ruled, Liu Wu was sent out to garrison the frontier and appointed Congjian as a memorial secretary in his staff.

sentences.zh: 從諫與師道諸奴日戲博交通，具知其陰密事，悉疏於悟，故悟得立功。

translations.literal: Congjian daily gambled and mingled with Shidao's servants, fully knowing their secret affairs and reporting all to Wu—thus Wu could achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian spent his days gambling and consorting with Li Shidao's household servants, learning all their secret dealings and reporting everything to Wu. It was thus that Wu was able to win his great victory.

sentences.zh: 悟卒，從諫知留後，持金幣賂當權者。

translations.literal: When Wu died, Congjian acted as acting commissioner and carried gold and gifts to bribe those in power.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wu died, Congjian took charge as acting commissioner and lavished gold and gifts on those in power at court.

sentences.zh: 朝議謂上黨內鎮，與河朔異，不可許。

translations.literal: Court debate held that Shangdang was an inner circuit, different from Hebei, and could not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that Shangdang was an inner circuit, unlike the Hebei provinces, and that succession could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 左僕射李絳奏言：「悟匿死，眾不必同亂，從諫威惠未著，若詔比鎮大將領節度，馳入軍，笮其未備，使軍情有屬，謀自屈矣。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Li Jiang memorialized: "Wu concealed death—the masses need not all rebel together. Congjian's authority and grace are not yet established. If a decree compares him to other circuits' great generals commanding the circuit, rush into the army, seize them unprepared, let army sentiment have allegiance—the plot will fold itself.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Li Jiang memorialized, "Wu concealed his death, but the troops need not all rise together. Congjian's authority and reputation are not yet established. If the throne issues a decree appointing a great general from another circuit as commissioner and sends him swiftly into the army while they are unprepared, the soldiers will have someone to follow and the plot will collapse of itself.

sentences.zh: 有如拒命，三州勢難獨存，數月可覆。」

translations.literal: If they refuse orders, the three prefectures' force can hardly stand alone—in months they can be overthrown."
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse the order, the three prefectures cannot long stand alone, and within a few months they can be overthrown."

sentences.zh: 時李逢吉、王守澄納其賂，數為請，敬宗乃以晉王為節度大使，詔從諫主留事，起將作監主簿，檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At that time Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng accepted his bribes and repeatedly petitioned; Jingzong then made the Prince of Jin grand commissioner, decreed Congjian manage acting affairs, raised him from Construction Supervisor registrar to acting Left Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Fengji and Wang Shoucheng had accepted Congjian's bribes and repeatedly interceded for him. Emperor Jingzong therefore made the Prince of Jin nominal commissioner, decreed that Congjian should manage affairs as acting commissioner, and raised him from registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings to acting Left Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 晉王帝所愛，從諫饋獻相望，未幾，拜節度使。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was the emperor's favorite; Congjian's gifts followed one after another, and before long he was appointed commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin was the emperor's favorite, and Congjian sent him gift after gift. Before long Congjian was formally appointed military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大和初，李聽敗館陶，走淺口，從諫引鐵騎黃頭郎救之，聽免。

translations.literal: Early in Dahe, Li Ting was defeated at Guantao and fled to Qiankou; Congjian led iron cavalry and yellow-head guards to rescue him, and Ting was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dahe reign, Li Ting was defeated at Guantao and fled to Qiankou. Congjian led his iron cavalry and yellow-cap guards to his rescue, but Li Ting was dismissed from command all the same.

sentences.zh: 進檢校尚書左僕射，拜司空，封沛國公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, appointed Minister of Works, and enfeoffed Duke of Pei State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, appointed Minister of Works, and enfeoffed as Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 昭義自悟時治邢州，而人思上黨，從諫還治潞。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi since Wu's time had governed from Xing Prefecture, but the people missed Shangdang; Congjian returned to govern from Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Wu's day the Zhaoyi command had been administered from Xing Prefecture, but the people longed for Shangdang. Congjian moved the seat of government back to Lu.

sentences.zh: 悟苛擾，從諫寬厚，故下益附。

translations.literal: Wu was harsh and turbulent; Congjian was generous and kind—thus subordinates attached themselves all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had been harsh and overbearing, whereas Congjian was generous and mild, and so his subordinates attached themselves to him all the more.

sentences.zh: 方年壯，思立功。

translations.literal: Still in the prime of life, he sought to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Still in the prime of life, he burned to win distinction.

sentences.zh: 六年，請入朝，文宗待遇加等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he requested audience at court; Wenzong received him with extra honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he requested an audience at court, and Emperor Wenzong received him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 明年，還藩，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next year he returned to his fief and was promoted to Grand Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to his command and was promoted to Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 公卿多托以私，又見事柄不一，遂心輕朝廷，有驕色。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers often entrusted private matters to him; he also saw power divided at court, and thus looked down on the court with an arrogant air.
translations.idiomatic: High officials often entrusted him with private favors, and seeing that power at court was divided, he came to look down on the throne and carried himself with arrogance.

sentences.zh: 李訓約從諫誅鄭註，及甘露事，宰相皆夷族，傳言死非其罪。

translations.literal: Li Xun plotted with Congjian to kill Zheng Zhu; when the Sweet Dew affair came, the chancellors were all exterminated, and rumor held they died without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun had plotted with Congjian to kill Zheng Zhu. When the Sweet Dew affair erupted, the chancellors were exterminated to the last man, and rumor held that they had died innocent of any crime.

sentences.zh: 從諫不平，三上書請王涯等罪，譏切中人。

translations.literal: Congjian was indignant; thrice he memorialized requesting the crimes of Wang Ya and others be reviewed, satirizing the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was outraged. Three times he memorialized the throne asking that the cases of Wang Ya and the others be reopened, his words cutting sharply at the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 時宦豎得誌，天子弱，鄭覃、李石新執政，藉其論執以立權綱，中人憚而怨之。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuchs had their way; the Son of Heaven was weak. Zheng Tan and Li Shi newly held power and borrowed his bold memorials to establish authority—the eunuchs feared and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs were then at the height of their power and the emperor was weak. The newly installed chief ministers Zheng Tan and Li Shi leaned on Congjian's bold memorials to reassert authority at court, while the eunuchs both feared and hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 又劾奏蕭本非太后弟。

translations.literal: He also impeached and memorialized that Xiao Ben was not the empress dowager's brother.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Xiao Ben, declaring that he was not the empress dowager's brother.

sentences.zh: 仇士良積怒，倡言從諫誌窺伺。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang accumulated rage and spread word that Congjian intended to watch and usurp.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang nursed his anger and spread word that Congjian harbored designs on the throne and was watching for his chance.

sentences.zh: 從諫亦妄言清君側，因與朝廷猜貳。

translations.literal: Congjian also rashly spoke of clearing the emperor's side, and thus mutual suspicion with the court.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian, for his part, rashly spoke of "purging evil from the emperor's side," and mutual suspicion between him and the court deepened.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，兼太子太師。

translations.literal: When Wuzong was enthroned, Congjian was additionally made Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Congjian was additionally appointed Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 性奢侈，飾居室輿馬。

translations.literal: By nature extravagant, he adorned his dwellings and carriages.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant, lavishing ornament on his residence and his horses and carriages.

sentences.zh: 無遠略，善貿易之算。

translations.literal: He had no far-reaching strategy but was skilled at trade calculations.
translations.idiomatic: He had no long view of statecraft but was adept at the arithmetic of commerce.

sentences.zh: 徙長子道入潞，歲榷馬征商人，又熬鹽，貨銅鐵，收緡十萬。

translations.literal: He moved his eldest son Dao into Lu; yearly he monopolized horses and taxed merchants, also boiled salt, sold copper and iron, and collected one hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his eldest son Li Dao into Lu Prefecture. Each year he monopolized the horse trade and levied taxes on merchants, boiled salt for sale, trafficked in copper and iron, and collected one hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 賈人子獻口馬金幣，即署牙將，使行賈州縣，所在暴橫沓貪，責子貸錢，吏不應命，即訴於從諫。

translations.literal: Merchants' sons offering horses and gold coins were immediately appointed yamen generals and sent trading through prefectures and counties; everywhere they were violent, greedy, and extortionate, demanding sons lend money—if officials did not obey, they complained to Congjian.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of merchants who offered horses and gold were immediately made yamen generals and sent to trade through the prefectures and counties. Everywhere they acted with violence and greed, extorting loans from local families. If an official refused them, they appealed straight to Congjian.

sentences.zh: 欲論奏，或遣客遊刺，故天下怨怒。

translations.literal: Those wishing to memorialize were sometimes sent wandering assassins—thus resentment and rage throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who tried to report them to the throne were sometimes hunted down by roaming assassins, and resentment spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 從諫畜馬高九尺，獻之帝，帝不納，疑士良所沮，怒殺馬，益不平。

translations.literal: Congjian kept a horse nine chi high, offered it to the emperor; the emperor did not accept it. Suspecting Shiliang had blocked it, he angrily killed the horse and grew more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian kept a horse nine feet tall at the withers and offered it to the emperor. When the emperor refused it, Congjian suspected Qiu Shiliang had blocked the gift. In rage he had the horse killed and grew all the more embittered.

sentences.zh: 又聞士良寵方渥，愈憂惑，欲自入朝，恐不脫禍，因被病，卒，年四十一，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Also hearing Shiliang's favor was just growing thick, he grew more worried and confused; wishing to enter court himself, he feared he could not escape disaster—thus he feigned illness, died, age forty-one, posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Qiu Shiliang's favor was growing ever stronger, his anxiety deepened. He wished to go to court in person but feared he would not escape harm. He therefore feigned illness, then died at the age of forty-one. He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 初，大將李萬江者，本退渾部，李抱玉送回紇，道太原，舉帳從至潞州，牧津梁寺，地美水草，馬如鴨而健，世所謂津梁種者，歲入馬價數百萬。

translations.literal: Initially, the great general Li Wanjiang was originally of the Turgesh tribe. Li Baoyu sent him back toward the Uyghurs; passing Taiyuan, the whole encampment followed to Lu Prefecture. He pastured at Jinliang Temple—the land beautiful in water and grass, horses like ducks and strong, the so-called Jinliang breed—yearly horse revenue several millions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been a great general named Li Wanjiang, originally of the Turgesh tribe. Li Baoyu had sent him back toward the Uyghurs, but passing Taiyuan his whole encampment followed him on to Lu Prefecture. He pastured his herds at Jinliang Temple, where the land was rich in water and grass and his horses—stocky as ducks yet powerful, the breed known as Jinliang horses—brought in several million in horse revenue each year.

sentences.zh: 子弟姻婭隸軍者四十八人，從諫徙山東，懼其重遷且生變，而子弟亦豪縱，少從諫，不甚禮，因誣其叛，夷三族，凡三百餘家。

translations.literal: Children, in-laws, and clansmen in the army numbered forty-eight. Congjian moved to Shandong, feared their heavy relocation would cause trouble, and the children were also arrogant and looked down on Congjian, not very respectful—thus he framed them for rebellion, exterminated three clans, over three hundred households in all.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-eight of his sons, sons-in-law, and clansmen served in the army. When Congjian moved east into Shandong he feared that relocating the Wanjiang clan would provoke trouble. The younger men were also proud and insolent, showed little respect for Congjian, and so he framed them for rebellion, exterminated three clans, and destroyed more than three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 姬妾有微過，輒殺之。

translations.literal: Concubines with minor faults—he immediately killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines who committed the slightest offense were killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 人皆知其將亡。

translations.literal: All knew he would perish.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew his end was near.

sentences.zh: 從子稹，父從素仕右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Nephew Zhen—his father Congsu served as Right Xiaowei General.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Li Zhen was the son of Li Congsu, who had served as a general of the Right Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 從諫以為嗣，病甚，與妻裴謀，令主軍事，置大將王協、郭誼、劉武德、劉守義等佐稹。

translations.literal: Congjian made him heir; gravely ill, he consulted with his wife Pei, had her manage military affairs, and appointed great generals Wang Xie, Guo Yi, Liu Wude, and Liu Shouyi to assist Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian designated him as his heir. When his illness grew grave, he consulted with his wife, Lady Pei, put her in charge of military affairs, and appointed the great generals Wang Xie, Guo Yi, Liu Wude, and Liu Shouyi to assist Li Zhen.

sentences.zh: 秘不發喪，協謀遣將姜岑請醫於朝。

translations.literal: They secretly did not announce mourning; Xie plotted to send general Jiang Cen to request a physician from court.
translations.idiomatic: They kept his death secret. Wang Xie then plotted to send the general Jiang Cen to the capital to request a court physician.

sentences.zh: 中人與醫至，時從諫死已再旬，稹曰：「公困革不任受詔，稹請代拜。」

translations.literal: The eunuch and physician arrived. By then Congjian had been dead for twenty days already. Zhen said: "The Duke is critically ill and cannot receive the edict; Zhen requests to bow on his behalf."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch and the physician arrived. By then Li Congjian had been dead for twenty days. Li Zhen said, "The Duke is critically ill and cannot receive the edict. Zhen asks to bow on his behalf."

sentences.zh: 中人曰：「臥而視可也。」

translations.literal: The eunuch said: "Viewing him while he lies abed will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch said, "It will do to view him as he lies in bed."

sentences.zh: 辭以母夫人侍，不可屏。

translations.literal: He declined on the grounds that his mother the Lady was in attendance and could not be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen declined on the grounds that his mother was attending the sickbed and could not be sent from the room.

sentences.zh: 中人欲直入，武德等戶之，中人恐有變，趨出，貺饋百萬。

translations.literal: The eunuch wished to enter directly. Wude and others guarded the door. The eunuch feared trouble, hurried out, and was sent off with a bribe of a million.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch tried to enter at once. Liu Wude and the others barred the door. Fearing a disturbance, the eunuch hurried out and was sent away with a bribe of a million cash.

sentences.zh: 後使者繼往，為知從諫已死者，未至數舍，眾懼，武德與將董可武出兵萬人迎勞，至牙門，不得前。

translations.literal: Later envoys went in succession. Learning Congjian was already dead, before they had gone a few lodges the crowd was afraid. Wude and the general Dong Kewu led ten thousand troops out to welcome and soothe them. At the headquarters gate they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Later envoys followed one after another. When they learned that Congjian was already dead, the men grew fearful before they had gone a few stages. Wude and the general Dong Kewu led ten thousand troops out to welcome and reassure them, but at the headquarters gate they were not allowed to advance.

sentences.zh: 諸將乃詣監軍崔士康邀說，請如河朔故事。

translations.literal: The generals then went to the army supervisor Cui Shikang to urge him, asking to follow the Hebei precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The generals then went to the army supervisor Cui Shikang to persuade him, asking that they follow the Hebei precedent.

sentences.zh: 士康懦，不敢拒，乃至喪次，扶出稹，為裹絁巾，曰：「毋更欲殺敕使。」

translations.literal: Shikang was timid and did not dare refuse. He then went to the mourning hall, helped Zhen out, wrapped a coarse-cloth headcloth on him, and said: "Do not again wish to kill the imperial envoys."
translations.idiomatic: Shikang was timid and did not dare refuse. He went to the mourning hall, helped Zhen out, wrapped a coarse cloth about his head, and said, "Do not again think of killing the imperial envoys."

sentences.zh: 諸將哄然笑，遂出見三軍。

translations.literal: The generals burst into roaring laughter, and then went out to appear before the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: The generals broke into loud laughter, then went out to appear before the entire army.

sentences.zh: 帝怒前使者不入，謫隸恭陵；

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that the earlier envoys had not entered, and banished them to serve at Gongling;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged that the earlier envoys had not been admitted and banished them to serve at Gongling;

sentences.zh: 稹所遣姜岑、梁叔文、梁叔明三輩，皆杖死京兆府。

translations.literal: The three parties Zhen had sent—Jiang Cen, Liang Shuwen, and Liang Shuming—were all beaten to death at the Capital Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The three men Zhen had sent—Jiang Cen, Liang Shuwen, and Liang Shuming—were all beaten to death in the Capital Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔從素書敕稹護喪還東都，稹不奉詔。

translations.literal: An edict written by Congsu ordered Zhen to convey the coffin back to the eastern capital; Zhen did not obey the decree.
translations.idiomatic: An edict penned by Li Congsu ordered Zhen to escort the coffin back to the eastern capital, but Zhen refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣議，李德裕建言：「稹所恃者，河朔耳。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the court ministers to deliberate. Li Deyu submitted a proposal: "What Zhen relies on is simply Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the court ministers to deliberate. Li Deyu submitted a proposal: "All Zhen relies on is Hebei.

sentences.zh: 若遣大臣諭上旨，出山東兵，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: If a senior minister is sent to expound the throne's intent, and troops from east of the mountains are mobilized, he will surely be broken."
translations.idiomatic: If a senior minister is sent to expound the throne's intent and troops from east of the mountains are mobilized, he will surely be broken."

sentences.zh: 有詔奪從諫、稹官，敕諸軍進討。

translations.literal: An edict was issued stripping Congjian and Zhen of their offices, and commanding all armies to advance against them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Congjian and Zhen of their offices and commanded all armies to advance against them.

sentences.zh: 於是河陽王茂元以兵屯萬善；

translations.literal: Then Wang Maoyuan of Heyang encamped at Wanshan with troops;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maoyuan of Heyang then encamped at Wanshan with his army;

sentences.zh: 河東劉沔守昂車關，壁榆社；

translations.literal: Liu Mian of Hedong held Angche Pass and fortified at Yushe;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian of Hedong held Angche Pass and fortified at Yushe;

sentences.zh: 魏博何弘敬柵肥鄉，侵平恩；

translations.literal: He Hongjing of Weibo palisaded at Feixiang and raided Ping'en;
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing of Weibo built palisades at Feixiang and raided Ping'en;

sentences.zh: 成德王元逵次臨洺，略任、堯山、向城；

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui of Chengde stationed at Linming and plundered Ren, Yaoshan, and Xiangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui of Chengde stationed at Linming and plundered Ren, Yaoshan, and Xiangcheng;

sentences.zh: 河中陳夷行營冀城，侵冀氏。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing of Hezhong encamped at Jicheng and raided Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing of Hezhong encamped at Jicheng and raided Jishi.

sentences.zh: 茂元別遣將營天井關，為賊將薛茂卿所破，執四將，火十七柵。

translations.literal: Maoyuan separately sent a general to encamp at Tianjing Pass. He was broken by the rebel general Xue Maoqing, who seized four generals and burned seventeen palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan separately sent a general to encamp at Tianjing Pass, but the rebel general Xue Maoqing defeated him, captured four generals, and burned seventeen palisades.

sentences.zh: 張巨進攻萬善，不能下。

translations.literal: Zhang Ju attacked Wanshan but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju attacked Wanshan but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 茂元欲走，會日暮，賊自潰去。

translations.literal: Maoyuan meant to flee, but at dusk the rebels broke and dispersed on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan was about to flee, but at dusk the rebels broke and scattered on their own.

sentences.zh: 詔忠武王宰以本軍入懷澤行營，陳許士票武，賊眾素憚畏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince Zhongwu Wang Zai to enter the Huai-Ze field headquarters with his own army. The soldiers of Chen and Xu were fierce in war, and the rebel masses had always dreaded and feared them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince Zhongwu Wang Zai to enter the Huai-Ze field headquarters with his own army. The Chen-Xu troops were fierce warriors, and the rebel masses had long dreaded and feared them.

sentences.zh: 而茂卿負戰勝，冀厚賞。

translations.literal: Maoqing, however, prided himself on his battle victories and hoped for a rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: Maoqing, however, took pride in his victories and hoped for a rich reward.

sentences.zh: 或言：「其兵犯王略深，朝廷且怒，節益不可至。」

translations.literal: Some said: "His troops have deeply violated the imperial domain; the court will soon be angered, and a commission will never come."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "His troops have deeply violated the imperial domain. The court will soon be angered, and a commission will never come."

sentences.zh: 稹然之，故茂卿大望，乃與宰通，即偽挑戰，亟北，委天井關去，左右七營皆潰。

translations.literal: Zhen agreed with this. Therefore Maoqing's expectations were great. He then communicated with Zai, feigned battle, fled north in haste, abandoned Tianjing Pass and left, and the seven camps on either flank all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen agreed. Maoqing's hopes therefore ran high. He then made contact with Wang Zai, feigned battle, fled north in haste, abandoned Tianjing Pass, and the seven camps on either flank all collapsed.

sentences.zh: 茂卿奔澤州，使諜言於宰曰：「澤可取，吾應於內。」

translations.literal: Maoqing fled to Ze Prefecture and sent a spy to tell Zai: "Ze can be taken; I will respond from within."
translations.idiomatic: Maoqing fled to Ze Prefecture and sent a spy to tell Wang Zai, "Ze can be taken. I will respond from within."

sentences.zh: 宰疑不進，失期，茂卿扼腕悵恨。

translations.literal: Zai suspected this and did not advance; missing the deadline, Maoqing wrung his wrists in frustration and regret.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai was suspicious and did not advance. Missing the agreed time, Maoqing wrung his wrists in frustration and regret.

sentences.zh: 稹聞其貳，召誅之。

translations.literal: When Zhen heard of his defection, he summoned and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen learned of his defection, he summoned Maoqing and executed him.

sentences.zh: 宰進破劉公直，拔陵川。

translations.literal: Zai advanced, defeated Liu Gongzhi, and captured Lingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai advanced, defeated Liu Gongzhi, and captured Lingchuan.

sentences.zh: 劉沔又取石會關。

translations.literal: Liu Mian also took Shihui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian also captured Shihui Pass.

sentences.zh: 李石代沔領河東，稹因石兄洺州刺史恬移書乞降，石以聞，右拾遺崔碣表請納之，帝怒，斥碣鄧城令，詔敢言罷兵者戮賊境。

translations.literal: Li Shi replaced Mian in command of Hedong. Zhen, through Shi's elder brother Tian, prefect of Mingzhou, sent a letter begging to surrender. Shi reported this. Right Reminder Cui Jie memorialized asking to accept the surrender. The emperor was enraged, demoted Jie to magistrate of Dengcheng, and decreed that whoever spoke of halting the campaign should be executed at the rebel border.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi replaced Liu Mian in command of Hedong. Zhen, through Shi's elder brother Li Tian, the prefect of Mingzhou, sent a letter begging to surrender. Li Shi reported this. Right Reminder Cui Jie memorialized asking that the surrender be accepted. The emperor was enraged, demoted Jie to magistrate of Dengcheng, and decreed that anyone who spoke of halting the campaign should be executed in rebel territory.

sentences.zh: 上令石答書許稹面縛，石馳往受之，稹不出。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shi to reply with a letter promising Zhen could surrender bound face-forward. Shi galloped to accept the surrender, but Zhen did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Li Shi to reply with a letter promising that Zhen could surrender with bound hands. Li Shi galloped to accept the surrender, but Zhen would not come out.

sentences.zh: 俄而太原將楊弁逐李石，與稹連和，稹諸將建議：「我求承襲，彼叛卒，若與之，是與反者。」

translations.literal: Before long the Taiyuan general Yang Bian drove out Li Shi and allied with Zhen. Zhen's generals advised: "We seek to inherit the command; they are mutinous soldiers—if we join with them, we join with rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Taiyuan general Yang Bian drove out Li Shi and allied with Zhen. Zhen's generals advised, "We seek to inherit the command lawfully. They are mutinous soldiers. If we join with them, we join with rebels."

sentences.zh: 械其使送京師，使康良佺屯鼓腰嶺，敗太原兵，生禽卒七百。

translations.literal: They shackled their envoy and sent him to the capital, sent Kang Liangqian to encamp at Guyao Ridge, defeated the Taiyuan troops, and captured seven hundred soldiers alive.
translations.idiomatic: They shackled the envoy and sent him to the capital, sent Kang Liangqian to encamp at Guyao Ridge, defeated the Taiyuan troops, and captured seven hundred soldiers alive.

sentences.zh: 帝猶不赦。

translations.literal: The emperor still would not pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still would not grant pardon.

sentences.zh: 始，從諫將死，命稹無笞辱群奴，故李士貴等與王協尤用事，士戰，有功不賞，下無鬥誌。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Congjian was near death, he had commanded Zhen not to flog or humiliate the household servants. Therefore Li Shigui and others, together with Wang Xie, wielded power especially. Soldiers fought in battle, but merit went unrewarded, and the ranks lost will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset, when Congjian was near death, he had commanded Zhen not to flog or humiliate the household servants. Li Shigui and others, together with Wang Xie, therefore wielded power above all others. When soldiers fought, merit went unrewarded, and the ranks lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 府中財貨尚山積，而協請稅商人，使劉溪等分出檢實，而溪並齊民閱其貲，十取二，百姓始怨。

translations.literal: The treasury goods in the commission still piled like mountains, yet Xie asked to tax merchants and sent Liu Xi and others to divide up and inspect holdings. Xi also grouped ordinary townspeople together to examine their wealth, taking two parts in ten, and the common people began to resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth in the commission treasury still piled like mountains, yet Wang Xie asked to tax merchants and sent Liu Xi and others to divide up districts and inspect holdings. Xi also lumped ordinary townspeople together to examine their wealth, taking two parts in ten, and the common people began to resent it.

sentences.zh: 從諫妻弟裴問守邢州，有募兵五百，號「夜飛將」，多豪姓子，其家以輸貲不時，為溪所囚。

translations.literal: Congjian's wife's younger brother Pei Wen guarded Xing Prefecture. He had five hundred recruited troops called the "Night-Flying Generals," mostly sons of great clans. Because their families did not deliver tax payments on time, they were imprisoned by Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian's wife's younger brother Pei Wen guarded Xing Prefecture. He had five hundred recruited troops called the "Night-Flying Generals," mostly sons of powerful clans. Because their families failed to deliver tax payments on time, Xi had them imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 問以為言，溪大怒，問因殺溪，與刺史崔嘏斬大將，自歸成德軍。

translations.literal: Wen spoke on their behalf. Xi was greatly enraged. Wen therefore killed Xi, and together with Prefect Cui Gu beheaded a senior general and surrendered himself to the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wen spoke on their behalf. Xi was furious. Wen therefore killed Xi, and together with the prefect Cui Gu beheaded a senior general and surrendered to the Chengde army.

sentences.zh: 王釗守洺州，給士㠿布一端，稹檄代歲稟。

translations.literal: Wang Zhao guarded Ming Prefecture and gave the soldiers one bolt of cloth. Zhen issued an edict replacing the annual grain ration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhao guarded Ming Prefecture and gave the soldiers one bolt of cloth. Zhen issued an edict replacing their annual grain ration.

sentences.zh: 釗謂眾曰：「庫物尚多，欲發以為賞，可乎？」

translations.literal: Zhao said to the troops: "Store goods remain abundant. Would you like to distribute them as rewards?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said to the troops, "The stores still hold plenty. Shall we distribute them as rewards?"

sentences.zh: 士皆喜。

translations.literal: The soldiers were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were delighted.

sentences.zh: 悉所有給之，送款魏博軍。

translations.literal: He gave them everything in the stores and sent terms of surrender to the Weibo army.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them everything in the stores and sent terms of surrender to the Weibo army.

sentences.zh: 礠州將高玉、堯山將魏元談等以次降成德，元逵以久為賊守，殺之。

translations.literal: Gao Yu, general of Ci Prefecture, Wei Yuanzan, general of Yaoshan, and others in succession surrendered to Chengde. Yuankui killed them because they had long served as rebel garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu, the general of Ci Prefecture, Wei Yuanzan, the general of Yaoshan, and others surrendered to Chengde one after another. Yuankui killed them because they had long served as rebel garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 稹聞三州降，大懼。

translations.literal: When Zhen heard that three prefectures had surrendered, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen learned that three prefectures had surrendered, he was terrified.

sentences.zh: 大將郭誼與王協始議圖稹，使董可武誘稹至北第，置酒，飲酣，即斬首，悉取從諫子在繈褓者二十餘，並從子積、匡周等殺之。

translations.literal: The grand general Guo Yi and Wang Xie first plotted against Zhen. They had Dong Kewu lure Zhen to the northern residence, set out wine, and when the drinking was heavy, beheaded him at once. They took more than twenty of Congjian's sons still in swaddling clothes, together with his nephews Ji, Kuangzhou, and others, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general Guo Yi and Wang Xie first plotted against Zhen. They had Dong Kewu lure Zhen to the northern residence, set out wine, and when the drinking was at its height, beheaded him at once. They took more than twenty of Congjian's sons still in swaddling clothes, together with his nephews Ji, Kuangzhou, and others, and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 誅張谷、張沿、陳揚庭、李仲京、王渥、王羽、韓茂章、茂實、賈庠、郭臺、甄戈十一族，夷之，軍中素不附者皆殺。

translations.literal: They executed the eleven clans of Zhang Gu, Zhang Yan, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Wang Wo, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang, Maoshi, Jia Xu, Guo Tai, and Zhen Ge, extirpating them to the roots, and killed all in the army who had never been loyal.
translations.idiomatic: They executed the eleven clans of Zhang Gu, Zhang Yan, Chen Yangting, Li Zhongjing, Wang Wo, Wang Yu, Han Maozhang, Maoshi, Jia Xu, Guo Tai, and Zhen Ge, exterminating them to the roots, and killed everyone in the army who had never been loyal.

sentences.zh: 函稹首送王宰，獻京師，告廟社，帝禦興安門受之。

translations.literal: They sent Zhen's head in a box to Wang Zai, who presented it to the capital, reported it at the temple and altars, and the emperor received it in state at Xing'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Zhen's head in a box to Wang Zai, who presented it to the capital, reported it at the temple and altars of state, and the emperor received it in state at Xing'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 劉公直亦降於宰。

translations.literal: Liu Gongzhi also surrendered to Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongzhi also surrendered to Wang Zai.

sentences.zh: 石雄以兵守境，軍大掠，誼移書責之，雄銜怒。

translations.literal: Shi Xiong held troops guarding the border; his army plundered greatly. Yi sent a letter rebuking him, and Xiong nursed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong held the border with troops, and his army plundered on a great scale. Guo Yi sent a letter rebuking him, and Xiong nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 稹之死，誼斥從諫妻伏夾室，收其貲私於己，建大廄，日望旌節。

translations.literal: After Zhen's death, Yi shut Congjian's wife in a side chamber, took her private wealth for himself, built a great stable, and daily looked for the arrival of a commander's insignia.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen's death, Guo Yi shut Congjian's wife in a side chamber, seized her private wealth for himself, built a great stable, and daily awaited the arrival of a commander's insignia.

sentences.zh: 宰相德裕建言：「稹庸下，亂繇誼始，及軍窮蹙，乃圖稹邀榮，不誅無以懲奸臣。

translations.literal: Chancellor Deyu submitted a proposal: "Zhen was base and inferior; the chaos began with Yi. When the army was cornered, only then did he plot against Zhen to seek glory. If he is not executed there is no way to punish treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Deyu submitted a proposal: "Zhen was base and inferior, but the chaos began with Guo Yi. When the army was cornered, only then did he plot against Zhen to win glory. If he is not executed, there is no way to punish treacherous ministers.

sentences.zh: 及兵在境，宜悉取逆黨送京師，論如法。」

translations.literal: Now that troops are at the border, all rebel partisans should be taken and sent to the capital to be judged according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Now that troops are at the border, all rebel partisans should be taken and sent to the capital to be judged according to law."

sentences.zh: 先是有狂人呼於潞市曰：「石雄七千人至矣！」

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a madman who cried in the Lu market: "Shi Xiong's seven thousand men have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a madman had cried in the Lu market, "Shi Xiong's seven thousand men have arrived!"

sentences.zh: 從諫捕誅之，乃請詔雄率兵如數以入。

translations.literal: Congjian had him captured and executed, then requested an edict for Xiong to lead that number of troops in.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congjian had him seized and executed, then requested an edict for Shi Xiong to lead that number of troops into Lu.

sentences.zh: 雄至潞，縛誼及王協、劉公直、安全慶、李道德、李佐堯、劉武德、董可武等送京師，並殊死。

translations.literal: When Xiong reached Lu, he bound Yi and Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Qingqing, Li Daode, Li Zuoyao, Liu Wude, Dong Kewu, and others and sent them to the capital; all were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Xiong reached Lu, he bound Guo Yi, Wang Xie, Liu Gongzhi, An Qingqing, Li Daode, Li Zuoyao, Liu Wude, Dong Kewu, and others and sent them to the capital. All were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 杖崔士康殺之。

translations.literal: Cui Shikang was beaten with the rod and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shikang was beaten with the rod and killed.

sentences.zh: 白惟信者，潞梟將，數與雄戰，懼不敢降，自武鄉殺都將康良佺，欲降盧鈞；

translations.literal: Bai Weixin was a fierce general of Lu who had fought Xiong many times; afraid, he did not dare surrender. From Wuxiang he killed the commander Kang Liangqian, intending to surrender to Lu Jun;
translations.idiomatic: Bai Weixin was a fierce Lu general who had fought Shi Xiong many times. Afraid, he did not dare surrender. From Wuxiang he killed the commander Kang Liangqian, intending to surrender to Lu Jun;

sentences.zh: 雄遣人召降，惟信殺之，卒降鈞。

translations.literal: Xiong sent men to summon his surrender. Weixin killed them and finally surrendered to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong sent men to summon his surrender. Weixin killed them and finally surrendered to Lu Jun.

sentences.zh: 有詔「從諫且死，乃署稹軍事，宜剖棺暴屍於市三日。」

translations.literal: There was an edict: "Since Congjian was about to die, Zhen was only then appointed to military affairs. His coffin should be opened and the corpse exposed in the market for three days."
translations.idiomatic: There was an edict: "Since Congjian was about to die, Zhen was only then appointed to military affairs. His coffin should be opened and the corpse exposed in the market for three days."

sentences.zh: 雄發視，面如生，一目尚開，雄三斬之，仇人剔其骨幾盡。

translations.literal: Xiong opened it and looked—the face was as if alive, one eye still open. Xiong struck it three times with a blade. Enemies scraped his bones nearly clean.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong opened the coffin and looked—the face was as if alive, one eye still open. Xiong struck it three times with a blade. Enemies scraped his bones nearly clean.

sentences.zh: 誼者，兗州人。

translations.literal: Guo Yi was a man of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi was a native of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄岌，事悟為牙將，常樂滏山秀峻，曰：「我死必葬此。」

translations.literal: His elder brother Ji served Wu as a headquarters guard and always loved the fine steepness of Fushan. He said: "When I die I shall surely be buried here."
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ji had served Liu Wu as a headquarters guard and always admired the fine steepness of Fushan. He said, "When I die I shall surely be buried here."

sentences.zh: 望氣者言：「其地當三世為都頭異姓。」

translations.literal: A geomancer said: "That ground will for three generations produce a commander of different surname."
translations.idiomatic: A geomancer said, "That ground will for three generations produce a commander of different surname."

sentences.zh: 河北謂都頭異姓，至貴稱也。

translations.literal: In Hebei they called such a commander of different surname the highest title of honor.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei they called such a commander of different surname the highest title of honor.

sentences.zh: 「然窆過二丈不利。」

translations.literal: "Yet if the burial is deeper than two zhang it will be unlucky."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet if the burial is deeper than two zhang it will be unlucky."

sentences.zh: 誼以岌假刺史，穿三丈，得石蛇並三卵，工破之，皆流血。

translations.literal: Yi, because Ji was acting prefect, dug three zhang and found a stone serpent together with three eggs. The workmen broke them open—all bled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi, because Ji was acting prefect, dug three zhang deep, they found a stone serpent together with three eggs. The workmen broke them open—all bled.

sentences.zh: 至是，誼及岌三子同誅。

translations.literal: At this time Yi and Ji's three sons were executed together.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Guo Yi and Ji's three sons were executed together.

sentences.zh: 張谷、張沿、陳揚庭皆有文，時時言古今成敗以佐從諫，故善遇此三人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gu, Zhang Yan, and Chen Yangting all had literary talent and often spoke of success and failure in past and present to assist Congjian, so he treated these three men well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gu, Zhang Yan, and Chen Yangting all had literary talent and often spoke of success and failure in past and present to assist Congjian, so he treated these three men well.

sentences.zh: 谷納邯鄲人李嚴女為侍人，號新聲。

translations.literal: Gu took as concubine the daughter of a Handan man, Li Yan, called Xinsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gu took as concubine the daughter of a Handan man named Li Yan, called Xinsheng.

sentences.zh: 當從諫潛圖窺脅，新聲諫谷曰：「始天子以從諫為節度，非有戰野攻城之功，直以其父挈齊十二州還天子，去就間未能奪其嗣耳。
