translations.literal: When Congjian was secretly plotting to usurp and coerce, Xinsheng admonished Gu: "At the beginning the Son of Heaven made Congjian commissioner not because he had merit in field battles or storming cities, but simply because his father brought the twelve prefectures of Qi back to the Son of Heaven—and at the moment of departure and return no one could wrest the succession from him.
translations.idiomatic: When Congjian was secretly plotting to usurp and coerce, Xinsheng admonished Gu: "At the beginning the Son of Heaven made Congjian commissioner not because he had merit in field battles or storming cities, but simply because his father brought the twelve Qi prefectures back to the Son of Heaven—and at the moment of departure and return no one could wrest the succession from him.

sentences.zh: 自有澤潞，未聞以一縷一蹄為天子壽，左右皆無賴。

translations.literal: Since there has been a Ze-Lu commission, never has one thread or one hoof been sent as birthday tribute for the Son of Heaven, and those at his side are all scoundrels.
translations.idiomatic: Since there has been a Ze-Lu commission, never has one thread or one hoof been sent as birthday tribute for the Son of Heaven, and those at his side are all scoundrels.

sentences.zh: 章武朝，數鎮顛覆，皆雄才傑器，尚不能固天子恩，況從諫擢自兒女手中，茍不以法得，亦宜以不法終。

translations.literal: In the Zhangwu reign several circuits were overthrown—all were men of heroic talent and outstanding ability, and even they could not secure the Son of Heaven's favor. How much less Congjian, raised up from the hands of women and children? If he did not obtain the command by law, he ought likewise to end by lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhangwu reign several circuits were overthrown—all were men of heroic talent and outstanding ability, and even they could not secure the Son of Heaven's favor. How much less Congjian, raised up from the hands of women and children? If he did not obtain the command by law, he ought likewise to end by lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 君當脫族西去，大丈夫勿顧一飯恩，以骨肉腥健兒食。」

translations.literal: You should leave clan and kin and go west. A true man should not cling to the kindness of a single meal and feed his flesh and blood to sturdy warriors."
translations.idiomatic: You should leave clan and kin and go west. A true man should not cling to the kindness of a single meal and feed his flesh and blood to sturdy warriors."

sentences.zh: 言訖悲涕。

translations.literal: When she finished speaking she wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When she finished speaking she wept in grief.

sentences.zh: 谷不決者三月，畏言泄，縊之。

translations.literal: Gu could not decide for three months. Fearing her words would leak out, he strangled her.
translations.idiomatic: Gu could not decide for three months. Fearing her words would leak out, he strangled her.

sentences.zh: 李仲京，訓之兄，為蕭洪府判官，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Li Zhongjing was the elder brother of Li Xun and served as aide in Xiao Hong's commission; he was promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongjing was the elder brother of Li Xun and served as aide in Xiao Hong's commission; he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 王渥，璠之子。

translations.literal: Wang Wo was the son of Wang Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wo was the son of Wang Fan.

sentences.zh: 王羽，涯族孫。

translations.literal: Wang Yu was a clansman of Wang Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu was a clansman of Wang Ya.

sentences.zh: 韓茂章、茂實，約之子。

translations.literal: Han Maozhang and Maoshi were sons of Han Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Maozhang and Maoshi were sons of Han Yue.

sentences.zh: 賈庠，餗子。

translations.literal: Jia Xu was the son of Jia Su.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xu was the son of Jia Su.

sentences.zh: 郭臺，行餘子。

translations.literal: Guo Tai was the son of Guo Xingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai was the son of Guo Xingyu.

sentences.zh: 甘露難作，皆羸服奔從諫，從諫衣食之。

translations.literal: When the Ganlu Affair broke out, they all fled in ragged clothes to Congjian, and Congjian clothed and fed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ganlu Affair broke out, they all fled in ragged clothes to Congjian, and Congjian clothed and fed them.

sentences.zh: 甄戈者，頗任俠，從諫厚給釁，坐上座，自稱荊卿。

translations.literal: Zhen Ge was quite chivalrous and bold. Congjian richly supplied him with sacrificial gifts, seated him in the place of honor, and styled himself Jing Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Ge was quite chivalrous and bold. Congjian richly supplied him with sacrificial gifts, seated him in the place of honor, and Ge styled himself Jing Ke.

sentences.zh: 從諫與定州戍將有嫌，命戈取之，因為逆旅上謁，留飲三日，乘間斬其首。

translations.literal: Congjian had a grudge with a garrison general of Ding Prefecture and ordered Ge to take his head. Ge therefore paid a respectful visit at an inn, kept him drinking for three days, and in an interval cut off his head.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian had a grudge with a garrison general of Ding Prefecture and ordered Ge to take his head. Ge therefore paid a respectful visit at an inn, kept him drinking for three days, and in an interval cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 它日，又使取仇人，乃引不逞者十餘輩劫之。

translations.literal: Another day he was again sent to take an enemy's head, but instead led more than ten desperadoes to rob him.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he was again sent to take an enemy's head, but instead led more than ten desperadoes to rob the man.

sentences.zh: 從諫不悅，號「偽荊卿。」

translations.literal: Congjian was displeased and called him "The false Jing Ke."
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was displeased and called him "The false Jing Ke."

sentences.zh: 從諫妻裴，以弟立功，詔欲貸其死。

translations.literal: Congjian's wife Pei—because her younger brother had achieved merit, an edict was about to pardon his death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian's wife Pei—because her younger brother had achieved merit, an edict was about to pardon his death sentence.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎劉三復執不可，於是賜死，以屍還問。

translations.literal: Vice Director of Punishments Liu Sanfu insisted it could not be allowed. Thereupon he was granted death by imperial favor, and the corpse was returned to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Punishments Liu Sanfu insisted it could not be allowed. Thereupon Wen was granted death by imperial favor, and the corpse was returned to him.

sentences.zh: 裴父敞，冕之裔，辟悟府，悟奇之，故為從諫納其女。

translations.literal: Pei's father Chang was a descendant of Pei Mian, entered Wu's staff, and Wu regarded him as remarkable—therefore he took his daughter for Congjian.
translations.idiomatic: Pei's father Chang was a descendant of Pei Mian. He entered Liu Wu's staff, and Wu regarded him as remarkable—therefore he took his daughter for Congjian.

sentences.zh: 裴年十五，火光起袿下，家人以為怪，因許婚。

translations.literal: When Pei was fifteen, fire-light rose from beneath her skirt. The family thought it strange and therefore agreed to the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei was fifteen, firelight rose from beneath her skirt. The family thought it strange and therefore agreed to the marriage.

sentences.zh: 封燕國夫人。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Lady of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: She was enfeoffed as Lady of Yan.

sentences.zh: 寬厚有謀，每勸從諫入朝為子孫計。

translations.literal: Broad-minded and resourceful, she often urged Congjian to enter court for the sake of his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded and resourceful, she often urged Congjian to enter court for the sake of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 從諫有妾韋願封夫人，許之，詔至，裴怒，毀詔不與。

translations.literal: Congjian had a concubine, Wei, who wished to be enfeoffed as a lady. He agreed. When the edict arrived, Pei was angry, tore up the edict, and would not give it to her.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian had a concubine, Wei, who wished to be enfeoffed as a lady. He agreed. When the edict arrived, Pei was angry, tore up the edict, and would not give it to her.

sentences.zh: 從諫它日會裴黨，復出詔，裴抵去，曰：「淄青李師古四世阻命，不聞側室封者。

translations.literal: Another day Congjian was feasting with Pei's faction and again produced the edict. Pei pushed it away and said: "In Ziqing, Li Shigu for four generations defied imperial orders—never was a concubine enfeoffed heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Congjian was feasting with Pei's faction and again produced the edict. Pei pushed it away and said, "In Ziqing, Li Shigu for four generations defied imperial orders—never was a concubine enfeoffed heard of.

sentences.zh: 君承朝廷姑息，宜自黜削，求洗濯，顧以婢為夫人，族不日滅耳！」

translations.literal: You enjoy the court's indulgence and ought to diminish yourself and seek cleansing. Yet you would make a maidservant a lady—the clan will perish before many days!"
translations.idiomatic: You enjoy the court's indulgence and ought to diminish yourself and seek cleansing. Yet you would make a maidservant a lady—the clan will perish before many days!"

sentences.zh: 從諫赧然止。

translations.literal: Congjian, abashed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian, abashed, stopped.

sentences.zh: 及韋至京師，乃言：「李丕降，裴會大將妻號哭曰：『為我語若夫，勿忘先公恩，願以子母托。』

translations.literal: When Wei reached the capital she said: "When Li Pi surrendered, Lady Pei met the senior generals' wives, weeping and wailing, and said: 'Tell your husbands for me—do not forget the grace of my late father-in-law; I beg to entrust mother and child to you.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wei reached the capital she said, "When Li Pi surrendered, Lady Pei met the senior generals' wives, weeping and wailing, and said, 'Tell your husbands for me—do not forget the grace of my late father-in-law. I beg to entrust mother and child to you.'

sentences.zh: 諸婦亦泣下，故潞諸將叛益堅。」

translations.literal: The other wives also shed tears, and therefore the generals of Lu rebelled all the more firmly."
translations.idiomatic: The other wives also shed tears, and therefore the generals of Lu rebelled all the more firmly."

sentences.zh: 由是及禍。

translations.literal: Thus they brought disaster upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: And so they met ruin.

sentences.zh: 初，術者李琢能言禍福，從諫以重幣邀，辟署大將。

translations.literal: Earlier the diviner Li Zhuo could speak of fortune and calamity; Congjian invited him with heavy gifts and appointed him a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the diviner Li Zhuo foretold fortune and disaster; Congjian courted him with rich gifts and made him a senior general.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，謂從諫曰：「往歲長星經鬥，公生直之。

translations.literal: Early in Huichang he told Congjian: "In years past the long comet crossed the Dipper—you were born under its direct influence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huichang he told Congjian, "Years ago the long comet crossed the Dipper—you were born straight under it.

sentences.zh: 今鎮復至，當有災。」

translations.literal: Now the comet has returned; calamity is due."
translations.idiomatic: Now the comet has returned—disaster is coming."

sentences.zh: 從諫即徙軍山東，開球場，鑿柳泉，大興役以厭。

translations.literal: Congjian at once moved his army east of the mountains, opened a ball court, dug the Willow Spring, and launched great public works to avert the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian promptly shifted his army east of the mountains, opened a ball ground, dug the Willow Spring, and launched huge public works to ward off the omen.

sentences.zh: 及病，有言琢所興造皆逆歲，疑有異謀，使稹數其罪殺之，府中洶洶，俄而李丕降。

translations.literal: When he fell ill some said Zhuo's constructions all ran counter to the year's cycle and suspected a plot; Zhen was made to list his crimes and kill him. The headquarters seethed, and soon Li Pi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Congjian grew ill, some said Zhuo's projects all violated the year's cycle and suspected treason; Zhen was ordered to charge and execute him. The headquarters erupted in uproar—and soon Li Pi defected.

sentences.zh: 有李佐之者，兼孫也，累調河南尉，號強直。

translations.literal: There was Li Zuozhi, a collateral grandson, repeatedly posted as magistrate of Henan and known as stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuozhi, a collateral grandson, had served repeatedly as magistrate of Henan and was known for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 嘗客潞，為從諫所禮，留不得去，遂署觀察府支使，因娶其從祖妹。

translations.literal: Once a guest at Lu, he was honored by Congjian, detained and not allowed to leave, then appointed aide in the observation office, and married a cousin on Congjian's mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been a guest at Lu; Congjian honored him and would not let him go, made him an aide in the observation office, and he married a cousin of Congjian's clan.

sentences.zh: 從諫薄疏屬，資媵寒闕，佐之亦薄之，不甚答。

translations.literal: Congjian slighted distant kin and provided his concubines meagerly; Zuozhi slighted them too and did not respond much.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian treated distant relatives coldly and stinted on his concubines' upkeep; Zuozhi slighted them as well and barely answered their appeals.

sentences.zh: 從諫病，佐之力諷使還東都，從諫雖不能從，然感服其言。

translations.literal: When Congjian fell ill Zuozhi strongly urged him to return to the eastern capital; Congjian could not comply but was moved and convinced by his words.
translations.idiomatic: When Congjian fell ill Zuozhi pressed him to go back to Luoyang; Congjian could not agree, yet he was moved by the counsel.

sentences.zh: 病且革，王協等恐佐之妻母有所關說，即輦母歸東都。

translations.literal: As the illness turned critical Wang Xie and the others feared Zuozhi's wife and mother might intervene, and at once sent the mother by carriage back to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness turned grave Wang Xie and his faction feared Zuozhi's wife and mother might lobby the court, and hurried the mother back to Luoyang by carriage.

sentences.zh: 會佐之奴告佐之交通賓客，漏軍中虛實，稹囚之。

translations.literal: Then Zuozhi's slave reported that Zuozhi trafficked with guests and leaked the army's true state; Zhen imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Then a servant accused Zuozhi of dealing with outsiders and leaking military secrets; Zhen had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 妻訴不見禮，稹遂殺之。

translations.literal: His wife pleaded that she had not been treated with courtesy; Zhen then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife protested that they had shown her no respect; Zhen had him executed.

sentences.zh: 武鄉令唐漢賓，儉裔孫，以稹拒命，固諫歸朝，不聽，舉族見害。

translations.literal: Tang Hanbin, magistrate of Wuxiang and a descendant of Jia Jian, because Zhen defied orders firmly admonished him to submit to the court; when he would not listen, Hanbin's whole clan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Hanbin of Wuxiang, a descendant of Jia Jian, urged Zhen to obey the court when he rebelled; ignored, he and his entire clan were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 李師晦者，本宗室子，始悟辟致幕府，見從諫稍恣橫，假言求長生術，不與事。

translations.literal: Li Shihui was originally of the imperial clan; Liu Wu summoned him to the staff. Seeing Congjian grow somewhat overbearing, he pretended to seek the art of long life and took no part in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shihui, born of the imperial clan, was brought into Liu Wu's staff. Seeing Congjian grow arrogant, he feigned interest in immortality lore and kept out of politics.

sentences.zh: 從諫使歸東都，師晦懼為谷、揚庭等所譖，請居涉，從諫不之疑。

translations.literal: When Congjian sent him back to the eastern capital Shihui feared slander by Gu and Yang Ting and asked to live at She; Congjian did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: When Congjian sent him to Luoyang Shihui feared denunciation by Gu and Yang Ting and asked to stay at She; Congjian suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 稹敗，有為帝言者，擢伊闕令，而贈薛茂卿博州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhen fell someone spoke for Shihui to the emperor; he was promoted to magistrate of Yique, and Xue Maoqing was posthumously made prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen's defeat someone spoke for Shihui at court; he was made magistrate of Yique, and Xue Maoqing was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 大中初，又贈漢賓本縣令。

translations.literal: Early in Dazhong Hanbin was also posthumously made magistrate of his home county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong Hanbin too was posthumously restored as magistrate of his home county.

sentences.zh: 先時，河北諸將死，皆先遣使吊祭，次冊贈，次近臣宣慰，度軍便宜乃與節，軍中不許出，乃用兵，大抵不半歲不能定，故謷將逆子皆得為之備。

translations.literal: Formerly when generals of Hebei died, envoys were first sent to mourn and sacrifice, then posthumous titles granted, then a close minister sent to console, and only after gauging the army's convenience was the commission given; troops were not allowed out until then, and only then were arms taken up—generally not settled within half a year, so arrogant generals and rebellious sons all had time to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when a Hebei general died the court first sent mourners, then posthumous honors, then a close minister to console the troops, and only after sizing up the army granted the commission; the army was kept in camp until arms were taken up—usually half a year before matters settled—so overbearing generals and rebellious heirs always had time to prepare.

sentences.zh: 稹初不意帝怒即見討，及茂元錄詔示稹，舉族號慟，欲自歸，而愚懦不決雲。

translations.literal: Zhen at first did not expect the emperor's wrath to bring immediate attack; when Maoyuan recorded the edict and showed Zhen, the whole clan wailed; he wished to surrender himself but was foolish and timid and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had not expected the emperor's anger to bring instant war; when Maoyuan read him the edict the clan wailed together. He wanted to submit but was too foolish and timid to decide.

sentences.zh: 自悟至稹三世，凡二十六年。

translations.literal: From Wu to Zhen were three generations, twenty-six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Liu Wu to Zhen were three generations spanning twenty-six years.

sentences.zh: 李丕者，善長短術，與從諫厚善，署大將。

translations.literal: Li Pi was skilled in prognostication by length; he was on close terms with Congjian and was appointed a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pi practiced divination by length; he was close to Congjian and made a senior general.

sentences.zh: 及稹阻命，軍中疾其才，丕懼，乞為遊弈深入，以圖營壁處，遂自歸。

translations.literal: When Zhen defied orders the army resented Pi's talent; Pi was afraid and begged to scout deep as a roaming patrol to locate camps and walls, then surrendered himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen rebelled the army envied Pi's ability; afraid, he asked to scout deep behind enemy lines to map camps and fortifications, then defected.

sentences.zh: 議者疑為賊遣，德裕奏言：「討賊半年，始有降者，當賞以勸餘。」

translations.literal: Critics suspected he had been sent by the rebels; Deyu memorialized: "We have fought the rebels half a year and only now have a defector—we should reward him to encourage the rest."
translations.idiomatic: Some suspected he was a rebel plant; Deyu wrote, "We have fought half a year with the first defector only now—reward him to encourage the others."

sentences.zh: 帝召見，擢忻州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and received him and promoted him to prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him and made him prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 丕請取榆社，東徑武安入討賊，雖邢、洺未下，而兵不得救潞。

translations.literal: Pi asked to take Yushe and enter east by Wuan to attack the rebels; though Xing and Ming were not yet taken, the enemy could not relieve Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Pi proposed taking Yushe and striking east through Wuan; even if Xing and Ming held out, rebel troops could not relieve Lu.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 楊弁亂，遣人誘丕，丕斬之，以兵扼走集。

translations.literal: When Yang Bian rebelled he sent men to entice Pi; Pi beheaded them and used his troops to block the escape routes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Bian rebelled he sent agents to win Pi over; Pi executed them and sealed the escape routes with his troops.

sentences.zh: 德裕言於帝曰：「度支戶部物積代州，今丕塞其路，賊破矣。」

translations.literal: Deyu told the emperor: "The revenue and treasury stores are piled at Daizhou; now Pi blocks the road—the rebels are broken."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu told the emperor, "Revenue and treasury stores are stacked at Daizhou—Pi now blocks the road and the rebels are finished."

sentences.zh: 乃趣丕討弁，兵未至而弁已禽。

translations.literal: He then urged Pi to attack Bian; the troops had not arrived when Bian was already captured.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Pi against Bian; before the army arrived Bian was already taken.

sentences.zh: 遷汾、晉二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Fen and Jin in turn.

sentences.zh: 大中初，拜振武節度使，檢校刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Early in Dazhong he was appointed Military Governor of Zhenwu and Acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong he received Zhenwu governorship and Acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 党項叛，徙鄜坊，卒。

translations.literal: When the Tangut rebelled he was moved to Zou-Fang and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut rose he was transferred to Zou-Fang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《傳》稱：「作《易》者其知盜乎！」

translations.literal: The commentator says: The *Tradition* states: "He who made the *Changes*—did he know thieves?"
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The Tradition says, "Did the maker of the Changes understand thieves?"

sentences.zh: 然則盜之情，非聖人不能知。

translations.literal: Thus the mind of a thief—none but a sage can know it.
translations.idiomatic: Only a sage can know what moves a thief's heart.

sentences.zh: 唐中衰，奸雄圜睨而奮，舉魏、趙、燕之地，莽為盜區，挐叛百年，夷狄其人，而不能復。

translations.literal: When Tang declined in its middle years, treacherous heroes glared round and rose; the lands of Wei, Zhao, and Yan became a wilderness of brigandage; rebellion was clutched for a century, the people barbarized, and the realm could not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Tang decline let ambitious men eye the realm and strike; Wei, Zhao, and Yan turned into bandit country; rebellion gripped the north for a century, the people were barbarized, and the court could not recover it.

sentences.zh: 昏上庸佐，惟不知盜故也。

translations.literal: Dim emperors and mediocre aides knew only that they did not understand thieves.
translations.idiomatic: Foolish emperors and mediocre ministers simply did not understand brigandage.

sentences.zh: 引妖就暝，以奪厥明，寧蕭俯、崔植等謂耶！

translations.literal: They drew demons toward dusk to steal its light—were not Ning, Xiao Fu, Cui Zhi, and the like such men!
translations.idiomatic: They beckoned demons into twilight to steal the daylight—were not men like Ning, Xiao Fu, and Cui Zhi exactly that!
